The agency contacted 40,844 households, 2451 teachers,  3161 members of VECs etc.  Survey was carried out using
both quantitative (primary survey using pre-tested beneficiary schedules) and qualitative (in-depth interview with
programme functionaries) techniques. The Committee is of the opinion that observations of CAG need to be looked into
seriously and shortcomings reported by them should be addressed suitably.  The Committee finds that unspent balances
under DPEP  amounting to Rs.1100.75 lakhs, Rs.3008.64 lakhs, 1351.61 lakhs and 5018.73 lakhs are lying with Bihar,
M.P., Orissa and U.P. respectively. This itself is an indication that DPEP is not functioning satisfactorily. (Para 7.5)
VIII     JANSHALA PROGRAMME
            The Committee is of the view that the  Scheme is in the initial stages of implementation and needs more time to
get the actual feedback about the scheme.  The Committee, however,  hopes that the observations made in the report of
the Bodh Shiksha Samiti will  help the Government in formulating its future strategy in regard to the Scheme.  (Para
8.3)
            As may be seen from the above, expenditure on the project in all the States is far from satisfactory.   The
Committee observes that implementation of the Scheme  in all the above States is very slow and urgent remedial
measures need to be taken by the Department as the scheme is scheduled to run for only 18 months more i.e. upto
March, 2003. (Para 8.4)
 
IX        MERGER OF SCHEMES:
            The Committee welcomes the initiative taken in this regard,  The Committee, however, recommends that all the
inherent flaws of the earlier schemes should not be reflected in the revised new schemes after merger of these
schemes            Therefore, the Committee  is of the view that wide ranging consultations  should be held with the State
Govts., who are the implementing authority before  arriving at a final decision. (Para 9.2)
X         SARVA SHIKSHA ABHIYAN
            The Committee recommends that provision for girls hostels especially in far flung areas should be made one of
the components  of SSA before it is implemented. (Para 10.5)
XI        GIRLS' EDUCATION
The Committee hopes that all these measures will help in promoting girl education, which is still elusive. (Para
11.5)
XII      EDUCATION OF SC/ST CHILDREN
            The Committee notes the ambitious interventions of the Government which have now become the part of Sarva
Shiksha Abhiyan, Since the SSA is still in initial stage of its implementation, the Committee can only hope that these
efforts will yield the desired result.  However, the Committee feels and recommends accordingly that such
blocks/districts where the tribal women literacy (as in the case of Orissa where it is merely 1.8 per cent) is much below
should be identified and given special attention in the implementation  of the scheme. (Para 12.5)

CHAPTER-I

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY
GOVERNEMNT

RECOMMENDATION

4.8 To start with, the Committee suggests that there is a need to optimize all existing and available
physical facilities to control overcrowding. The Committee would emphasise the necessity for
opening more counters and creating space for OPD patients. Since overcrowding also results वीणा
lack of guidance and direction to patients and a patient friendly handling system, there is a need for
constant review of arrangements as to how for appropriate information and guidance are available to
patients and their relatives visiting the hospitals. In particular, constant vigilance is needed for a better
interface between clerical staff and patients visiting the hospitals.

ACTION TAKEN

4.8 The Ministry agrees with the observations. Hospitals are taking steps to ensure that proper
guidance and directions are given to patients, further that efforts are made for rationalizing the use of
space.

RECOMMENDATION

4.10 Another solution in this connection, according to the Committee, could be setting up of the OPDs
away from the main wing of the hospital, preferably in the same complex, with self-contained
essential test/diagnostic facilities to divert the patients seeking OPD attention from those needing
detailed investigation and treatment. The Committee is happy to learn that the AIIMS is already in the
process of setting up such OPD, away from the main hospital area, which would be provided essential
facilities for basic pathological tests required for primary care. Such OPDs, the Committee feels,
would not only reduce the congestion in the main hospital, but it would also release some working
space for physicians, etc.

ACTION TAKEN

4.10 The suggestion to set up OPDs away from the main wing of the hospitals will be kept in view
while considering the establishment of new OPDs as also the need for providing essential facilities
within easy reach to provide basic care quickly.

studying the pattern of patients. An overall goal in each hospital could be to strive to reach a situation

4.13 With the growth of technology, more and more sophisticated tests would be needed to support

duty of the leaders in the profession, especially those heading the Departments, to examine and assess,

equitably addressed. The Committee recognizes, therefore, that overcrowding may be reduced only by
a simultaneous improvement in (a) the levels of management efficiency in hospitals, (b) improvement
in peripheral facilities in District and State hospitals for primary and secondary treatment, and (c)

4.7 The Ministry agrees with the observations. Construction of peripheral hospitals by the
Government of NCT of Delhi is expected to reduce pressure on the Central Government hospitals.
Government of NCT of Delhi has informed that additional Central assistance amounting to Rs.1 crore
was approved for Pilot Project for effective Health Delivery system in Trans Yamuna area.

This was done in view of the various health and environmental hazards being faced by the
residents of East Delhi, comprising one third of the total population of Delhi. The people of East
Delhi face challenges of inadequate supply of safe drinking water, improper disposal of liquid and
solid waste, vehicular pollution of air and poor health care facilities. Poverty, low literacy rate,
unplanned colonization, lack of health consciousness among masses and lack of education has further
contributed to the poor health status of the community.

A baseline survey has been got conducted by Delhi Government in Trans Yamuna area
through ICMR for assessing health need and baseline data of various health indicators and socio-
economic status of the people of Trans Yamuna Area, so that proper infrastructure can be developed
for providing primary health care including strengthening of lab. Services and to develop a proper
referral system by identifying secondary level health care institutions and tertiary health care
institutions under 3 Tier health care delivery system in future, as per the objectives of the pilot project
for which funds had been initially allocated.

The ICMR has already submitted the interim report of the baseline survey and the final report is yet
to be received. The total amount of Rs.20.5 lakhs had been spent for this purpose. Keeping in view
the establishment of three-tier referral system, the following have been initiated in subsequent years
till now.

At primary health care level, 7 health centers have already been opened in Trans Yamuna Area with

For tertiary health care services, 5.39 hectors of land had been purchased at Tahirpur for 650 bedded

Since its inception, the Institute has been continuously developing and evolving curricular strategies

Earlier the duration of the first professional phase of MBBS _ course in all medical colleges used to

The Committee has been given to understand that number of OPD registration

in premier hospital like PGIMER, Chandigarh and AIIMS, New Delhi. The experience of PGI,

practical difficulties, the Committee is of the view that there must be a clear objective to make them

and expects that appropriate mechanism would be developed to achicve this

The Committee notes that some progress in computerisation has been made so far as

Hospitals at the earliest. Adequate funds should be made available by the Central Govt. for

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee has been informed that a Control Room has been set up since 1996 in

RECOMMENDATION

10. The Committee noted that the equipments available in different hospitals have not been properly
maintained. Repairs are not done promptly when they go out of order. The Committee feels that the
maintenance of equipments is very crucial as the patients face lots of problems if the equipments are
not repaired in time. They are fleeced by private labs/diagnostic clinics which charge exorbitant
amounts even for routine and normal tests. It has come to the notice of the Committee that patients are
referred to private labs/diagnostic centers for various tests on the pretext of equipments in the hospitals
being out of order and private diagnostic centers are allowed to import medical equipments at

providing necessary infrastructure for getting the medical equipments repaired in a reasonable time.

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

maintained/repaired timely or sophisticated equipments lying unutilised. | The Committee
strongly feels that there is an urgent need for evolving an affective monitoring mechanism to
check such instances both at the hospital level and in the Department. Appropriate action in
this regard should be taken at the earliest.

RECOMMENDATION

12. The Committee is disappointed over the fact that the functioning of the family welfare units, in
almost all the hospitals visited by it, was very poor. For example, in PGIMER only five vasectomies

our social-economic development. It, therefore, recommends that family welfare units provided in the

laid on vasectomy as family welfare device and suitable incentive/motivations be provided.

16. The Committee found that cleanliness and hygiene in various hospitals are very poor. Choked

such state of affairs as stagnated water and open garbage become breeding grounds for various
organisms. The Committee feels that hospital authorities are not paying adequate attention to this
aspect and recommends that immediate steps be taken to keep the hospitals clean and hygienic.

The Committee feels that even though some steps have been taken, a lot more needs to be
done _ in the area of cleanliness and hygiene in the hospitals. The action taken is not visible in

Department. The Department may appoint a Committee of experts to examine the present state of

19. The Committee received a number of complaints about the rude behaviour of a section of doctors
and staff towards patients and of lower staff with doctors. It also noticed that, ‘generally, the

19.2 The Committee, therefore, feels that deterrent punishment, coupled with an efficient grievances
redressal system/mechanism like JCMs in government establishments. should be provided in each

19.3 The Committee would also recommend early redefinition of the role and functions of Hospital
Management Boards. Norntally, these boards are intended to be responsible for smooth functioning of

44


fact that they are often (as in AIIMS) composed solely of those responsible for providing hospital

The Delhi Government has not set up any Geriatric Clinics separately. However, Special Clinics on

24. The Committee is deeply concerned about inadequate facilities for treatment of poor patients for
major illnesses, especially those involving various complicated procedures. The Committee has noted
that (a) several major invasive procedures, ¢.g. cardiac surgery are too expensive for the poor people
(unaffordable even for middle class); (b) there is a wide disparity, amounting to almost a factor | to 3,
between private and public hospitals, even at the lowest priced public hospitals. For most of these life
conditions, the patient has to produce substantial private funds even after contributions are received
from the PM’s and CM’s relief fund, etc. and (c) the costs are unlikely to come down soon.

ACTION TAKEN

24. National Illness Assistance Fund has been set up with an initial contribution of Rs.5 crores. The
fund could be subscribed by individuals in India or abroad, corporate: bodies in private or public
sector, philanthropic organization and all contributions made to this fund is exempt from payment of
Income Tax under Section 80-G of Income Tax Act. The primary objective of the fund is to provide
financial assistance to patients living in States/ Union Territories, below poverty line in India,
suffering from major life threatening diseases, to receive medical treatment at any of the
superspeciality Hospitals/Institutes or other Government/Private hospitals. The financial assistance to
such patients would be released in the form of a one-time grant which will be released to the Medical
Superintendents of the hospitals in which the treatment has been/is being received. In a bid to speed
up the assistance to the needy patients, the scheme has been modified in January, 1998 to provide that

RECOMMENDATION

24.1 While a point of view was expressed by some witnesses that procedure may not be a likely
priority for the poor, the Committee is not impressed with this argument. Urbanisation and its
attendant problems, considerable adulteration in food and drugs, tensions of a competitive modern life,
etc. are some trends increasingly affecting the rich and the poor alike, except that the poor are subject
to the double jeopardy of exposure to both infectious and non-communicable diseases. Therefore, the
Committee would suggest that the Ministry must urgently explore all appropriate sources of funds to
assist poor patients coming to AIIMS or other Central Government hospitals for treatment of specific
life threatening illness. If a mechanism can be set up, such as a National Catastrophic Illness
Assistance Fund, then resources can flow from all sources, including private charities and international
agencies and organisations. Besides, there can be many imaginative methods of requiring both
government and private hospitals of a certain size and even profit-making nursing homes to make
earmarked contributions to the fund. Procedures would, of course, have to be developed to create a
decentralized self regulating network of major participating hospitals to have early and quick help to
poor patients.

open space on the left side of the main Institute building, lving vacant. The Committee is of the
opinion that the space could be utilised for physical expansion of the Institute. The committee is also
of the opinion that the old building in which the workshops are being run, can be demolished and a
multi-storeyed building can be constructed where some of the Departments can also be shifted.

AIP 7.1 The Committee was informed that a proposal for constructing a building had already been
finalised and an amount of Rs.50 lakhs was provided for this purpose. It, however. could not be
utilised as the Planning Commission did not approve it. Planning and designing process also had taken
a longer time because the architect was Delhi-based and had to come to Bombay for this purpose. In
view of the acute shortage of space and accommodation. the Committee recommends that the
Department should get the necessary approval in this regard from the Planning Commission at the
earliest. Appointing an Architect based in Bombay or taking the help of CPWD, Bombay, should also
be considered.

ACTION TAKEN
7. The construction of Annexe Building started on 29.9.2000. The construction work is in full swing.

Foundation and plinth work has been completed. Super structure work is under progress. The
construction of the building is expected to be completed by August. 2002.


OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS AT A GLANCE

CHAPTER-III

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF
THE GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee notes the various steps taken /proposed for augmentation of health
services in the NCT of Delhi. The Committee is, however, apprehensive that the envisaged plan
may not be completed in the Tenth Five Year Plan. While agreeing that the Central
Government can only supplement the medical facilities provided by the State Governments, the
Committee wishes to point out that due to financial constraints, the required health system is
missing in the States. The Committee has been informed that Schemes like setting up of Local
Self-Government Dispensaries , developing of Regional Diagnostic Centres , World Bank aided
State Health System Development Projects etc. have been initiated by the Central Government.
The Committee hopes that these steps would result in a better medicare system in the States
which would gradually lessen the burden of Central Govt. Hospitals. The Committee would,
however, emphasise that the Central Govt. should constantly monitor the medical facilities being
provided in the States, specially the adjoining States of the Capital. ( Para 4.3&4.4)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee desires that all necessary steps may be taken to finalise and implement
the Comprehensive Re-development Plan in time for LHMC and Associated hospitals and
complete the construction of additional buildings in Dr. RML hospital and A and D wings of
OPD complex in Safdarjung hospital at the earliest. (Para 4.5)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee strongly recommends that the Department get the necessary approvals
from the civic authorities of Delhi, at the earliest, so that early construction of screening OPD at
AIIMS can be taken up as the matter is hanging on fire for the last so many years and the ever-
increasing patient load is adversely affecting the patient care and research activities of the
Institute. (Para 4.6)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is not inclined to agree with the views of the Department that the entire
responsibility of developing peripheral hospitals lies with the State Governments. The
Committee is, therefore, of the view that a comprehensive plan to develop primary and
secondary health care services which are most neglected by many States may be chalked out i:
consultation with the State Govts. at the highest level and a time frame to implement the plan
may be set. Special emphasis may be given for this aspect in the 10" Plan. (Para 4.9)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee recommends that immediate steps should be taken to
computerise the OPD registration in all the Central Govt. Hospitals as being done in
JIPMER, Pondicherry. The Committee is also of the view that separate queues for
senior citizens should be made mandatory in all the Central Govt. Hospitals. (Para 4.12)

72



COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is, however, of the view that all necessary steps should be taken to
maintain the referral character of these Institutes. The Committee would be interested to know
the details of papers read in national as well as international seminars and published.

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee notes that some progress in computerisation has been made so far as
Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. R.M.L. Hospital and AIIMS are concerned. The Committee would,
however, like to emphasise that efforts should be made to fully computerise all the Central Govt.
Hospitals at the earliest. Adequate funds should be made available by the Central Govt. for
this purpose. (Para 6) ..

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is, however, constrained to point-out that these facilities are only on
paper. Instances of precious lives being lost due to some vital equipment being non-functional
continue to occur on a regular basis. Reality is that only those patients whose attendants can
manage some reference at the right place get the best medicare. The Committee is of the view
that such control rooms and coordination between the hospitals should be activated. Surprise
inspections by higher authorities can prove to be effective in this matter. (Para 8)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is not inclined to agree with the contention of the Department that the
present system of entering into annual repair/maintenance contract ensures Departmental
responsibility. Reports continue to come about there being instances of equipments not being
maintained/repaired timely or sophisticated equipments lying unutilised. The Committee
strongly feels that there is an urgent need for evolving an affective monitoring mechanism to
check such instances. both at the hospital level and in the Department. Appropriate action in
this regard should be taken at the earliest. (Para 10) :

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee notes that a Technical Committee headed by DGHS had given specific
recommendations with regard to treatment facilities of epilepsy patients in its Report submitted
in September, 1996. The Committee is, however, surprised to find that no follow-up action
seems to have been taken as comments from the concerned authorities are still awaited. The
Committee is of the opinion that the Department should vigorously pursue this issue so that the
requisite action is taken at the earliest. (Para 14.1)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee feels that even though some steps have been taken, a lot more needs to be
done in the area of cleanliness and hygiene in the hospitals. The action taken is not visible in
reality. There is absolute lack of coordination between the local bodies and hospital authorities
in removing waste from the hospitals. The Committee is, therefore, of the view that there is need
for regular and proper interaction between the two authorities. ©The Committee is also of the
view that M/o Environment and Forests has a special role to play in waste management. The
Committee desires that the Department should take up the issue of waste management
vigorously. हु

73


The Committee finds that the Ministry of Labour has permitted for relaxation of rule for
engaging private contractual labour for sanitation work of Dr. R.M.L. Hospital, Safdarjung
Hospital and Lady Hardinge Medical College and Associated Hospitals for the period upto
February,2002. The Committee has been given to understand that contract labourers are
engaged for sanitation work in Safdarjung Hospital and the experience is found to be
satisfactory. Similar proposal for Dr. RML Hospital and LHMC is under process. The
Committee hopes that Ministry of Labour has extended the permission for relaxation of rule
beyond February, 2002. (Para 16)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee finds that the Ministry of Urban Affairs and Employment seems to have
reservation on the issue of transfer of administrative control of CPWD units posted in the
hospitals to the Medical Superintendents. The Committee is of the strong opinion that for a
proper maintenance of hospital buildings, CPWD units should be placed under the direct
supervision of Medical Superintendents. _If that is not done, procedural delays would continue
to occur and upkeep of hospital buildings would remain unsatisfactory. The Committee,
therefore, reiterates that the Department should again pursue this issue with the Ministry of
Urban Affairs and Employment. (Para 16.1)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITEE

The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Department. The Committee feels
that creation of Group C&D posts does not'commensurate with the work load. The Committee
desires that the process of creation of posts in Group C&D may be completed without any
further delay to provide efficient and quality service to the patients. (Para 17.2)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee feels that the present system of Public Grievances Committee addressing
the complaints of patients is not working satisfactorily because the Doctors themselves are
members of the Committee against whom complaints are made. |The Committee therefore,
reiterates its recommendation for creation of 'Ombudsman' type of machinery. The Committee
is constrained to point out that there is absence of work culture in the medical staff of the
Government hospitals. They are often found lacking in polite behaviour, reception,
responsiveness and discipline. The Committee, therefore, strongly feels that there is an urgent
need of change in work culture among medical staff. In this connection, the Department may
take necessary steps to include attitudinal training in the in-service training programme of
health workers. (Para 19.2)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
The Committee is not inclined to agree with this viewpoint. The Committee reiterates

that effectiveness and objectivity of the Hospital Management Boards will only be there if
besides hospital functionaries, outsiders are also made their members. (Para 19.3)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is not happy to note that the proposal of setting up of Geriatric clinics is
still under examination of the Department even after expiry of more than six years and it has not
been able to take a decision regarding setting up of such clinics. The Committee expects the
Department to take an early decision in this matter. (Para 23)

74


COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee feels that the states which have not set up National Illness Assistance
Fund may be persuaded to set up the Fund at the earliest, so that the poor patients living in
these states are able to take benefit out of the Fund. The Committee notes that even though the
Fund is in existence for quite some time not many poor patients are aware of its existence. The
Committee, therefore, desires that adequate publicity through the electronic/print media may
be given about this Fund. (Para 24)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is constrained to point out that public is not aware about the provision
regarding exemption of poor and indigent patients from payment of diagnostic and laboratory
service charges in Central Government Hospitals . The Committee, therefore, recommends that
steps should be taken for giving wide publicity through the electronic and print media. Such
information should also be made available at the Enquiry Counters of Central Government
Hospitals so that needy patients can take the maximum benefit. (Para 24.1)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee observes that a number of Projects for providing accommodation
facilities to attendants accompanying the patients coming from outside Delhi have been
approved and are in various stages of implementation in Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. RML
Hospital, LHMC and AIIMS. The Committee recommends that all efforts should be made to
expedite the completion of these Projects. The Department may also explore the possibility of
augmenting these facilities wherever feasible. (25.1)

ALL INDIA INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES, NEW DELHI
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is deeply disturbed to note the reply of the Department that AIIMS
which is a premier institute of the country is neither able to provide dialysis facility to all
patients approaching it nor is currently in a position to cope with the requirements of life long
dialysis for chronically ill patients on a long term basis. The Committee feels that while the
Department feels the necessity of strengthening the Nephrology unit, it is not serious in action.

The Committee, therefore, recommends that the existing Nephrology unit of the hospital
should be strengthened in terms of space, equipment and staff etc. at the earliest.(16.1&16.2)

POSTGRADUATE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH
(PGIMER), CHANDIGARH

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Department is silent about the Committee's recommendation with regard to revival
of JCM in the Institute. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its earlier recommendation that
the JCM be revived without further delay, if not already done. (Para 16 & 16.1)

JAWAHARLAL INSTITUTE OF POSTGRADUATE MEDICAL
EDUCATION & RESEARCH, PONDICHERRY
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee expresses its displeasure over the undue delay in the matter. It finds
that the proposal is still being processed at different levels. The Committee recommends that

75


the proposal may be finalized and implemented without further loss of time under intimation to
it. (Para 5)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is not in a position to understand why the employees are opposing the
grant of autonomy. The Committee feels that the Department may make all out efforts to allay
their fears about the issue of autonomy and convince them about the necessity of granting
autonomy. It hopes that a consensus would be reached soon. (Para 8)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

Though the Institute has taken some steps in this regard as compared to the staff
strength, the Committee, feels the additions made are miniscule. It desires that steps may be
taken to construct more quarters inside the campus itself. (Para 9)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee takes a serious view of the matter. The Committee would like to be
apprised of the reasons for delay in non notification of draft Recruitment Rules and how does
the Department propose to fill up the posts in the absence of these rules. It also desires that the
Recruitment Rules are notified without further delay. (Para 11.2)

SAFDARJUNG HOSPITAL
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is shocked to note that the authorities are not even aware, who is the
owner of the land, while they were pursuing the things with the M/o Defence and precious time
has been wasted in this futile exercise. The Committee is equally perturbed to note that money
has already been deposited for the said land, and the matter is still hanging on fire. The
Committee feels that the matter may be taken up on a regular basis at the highest level with
M/o Urban Development to hand over the possession of land without further delay since five
years have elapsed after the decision of the Committee of Secretaries. ( Para 6)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is perturbed by this casual approach and fails to understand the reasons
for envisaging a scheme in the early days of a Pian period, doing some preliminary exercise and
by the end of the Plan , simply dropping the proposal. (Para 17.1)
DR. RAM MANOHAR LOHIA HOSPITAL
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee desires that the matter may be pursued vigorously at the appropriate
level. (Para 5.3)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee expresses its dismay over the lukewarm approach of the Department.
The Department has failed to procure necessary equipment for improving the Burns and Plasti:

76



ward even after more than six years. The Committee desires that necessary action in this regard
may be taken without further loss of time. (Para 6)

LADY HARDING MEDICAL COLLEGE AND ASSOCIATE HOSPITAL
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee would like to be specifically apprised whether the entire encroachment
in the vicinity of the Hospital has since been removed. (Para 2.3)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee notes the reply of the Department. The Committee, however, is
skeptical whether all the lacunae in the hospital can be remedied by implementing the
Comprehensive Development Plan. Moreover, the Plan is in conceptual stage and will be
implemented in stages and some of the issues require immediate attention. Further, no time
frame has been set by the Department to start and complete the Plan. (Para 12.2)

ALL INDIA INSTITUTE OF PHYSICAL MEDICINE & REHABILITATION
(AIIPMER), BOMBAY.

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Department. The report of the
Committee was submitted in 1995, while the proposal was sent to M/o Finance in March, 1999.
The Committee regrets to note that nearly after four years the proposal was sent. If
immediate action had been initiated, the present situation could have been avoided. (Para 3.1)

COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE

The Committee notes the reply. However, the position would not have improved much
where in all the employees would have got residential accommodation. The Committee,
therefore, reiterates the recommendation made in its 31* Report. (Para 4)

informed the Committee about the various steps taken by the Govt., from time to time, to improve the

REPORT
I.          INTRODUCTION
1.1       Main objectives of the Department of Health are :
(i)
                  to undertake national programmes of health and to intensify measures for the prevention, control and
eradication of communicable diseases;
(ii)                to promote education, research and training in various medical disciplines, to reorient the medical
colleges in the delivery of health services in rural areas;
(iii)               to prevent adulteration of food as well as drugs;
(iv)              to provide primary health care at the doorsteps of the people and to train the required number of
personnel for this purpose;
(v)                to take steps for better implementation of Health Care Programmes for tribal and other weaker sections
of the Society; and
(vi)              to collaborate with member countries of United Nations and International Agencies like WHO, UNICEF
in matters relating to health promotion.
1.2              The Department of Health incurs expenditure either directly or through various institutions and establishments
run by it and by way of grants given to autonomous and voluntary organizations.  Grants to States and Union Territory
Administrations are mainly for Centrally Sponsored Health Schemes being implemented thorough the State
Governments and Union Territory Administrations.  They include national programmes for prevention, control and
eradication of diseases.
1.3              The Department finances, wholly or substantially, the following autonomous Institutions engaged in patient care

II          BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
2.1       Plan allocation for the Department of Health for 2002-03 is Rs. 1550.00 crores  showing an increase of 7% over
the Plan allocation of Rs. 1450.00  crores for 2001-02.  On a specific query  about the projected demand of the
Department for 2002-03, the Committee was informed that a plan outlay of Rs. 2009.60  crores was proposed.  
Additional allocation was meant for new initiatives emanating from the draft National Health Policy-2002, such as
distributing drugs to Primary Health Centres, Urban Health, setting up of a Medical Grants Commission.   The
Committee was, however,  given  to understand that the meager increase in 2002-03 would not be sufficient even for
maintaining the tempo of the existing programmes.
2.2       The Committee has observed that during the Ninth Plan period, every year Plan allocation has been less than the
projected demand of the Department, which has been  reduced without a break at the RE stage and even that reduced
allocation continued to remain under-utilised.  The Committee has been informed that major shortfall in expenditure
during the initial years of Ninth Plan was due to non-finalisation of procedural formalities observed in the case of
National Anti-Malaria Programme and National TB Control Programme.   Utilization of funds increased from 55% in 
1998-99 to 88% in    2000-01.   The Committee is, however, not fully inclined to agree with the explanation given by
the Department.   The Committee observes that the trend of under-utilisation has continued during the Ninth Plan  due to
variety  of reasons like non-setting up of required infrastructure  for implementation of various disease control
programmes, non-release of funds due to unspent balances lying with the implementing agencies, slow performance of
district societies, less number of proposals from NGOs, non-completion of required formalities etc.   During 2001-02,
the last year of Ninth Plan, Plan allocation of Rs. 1450.00 crores was reduced to Rs. 1320.00 crores at the RE stage, and
anticipated expenditure at the end of the year is Rs. 1300.00 crores.   The Committee hopes that all procedural
formalities under ongoing  and proposed Programmes/Projects during Tenth Plan have been completed so that optimum
and judicious utilization of allocated funds is ensured right from 2002-03, the first year of Tenth Plan. 
III.       CENTRAL   GOVERNMENT   HEALTH   SCHEME
3.1
              The Scheme was started in 1954 with the objective of providing comprehensive medical care facilities to
Central Government employees and their family members.  The Scheme which initially started in Delhi now covers 23
cities of which Bhubaneswar and Ranchi CGHS cater only to staff of Accountant General posted there and their
pensioners.
3.2
              Rs. 12.00 crores under plan has been  provided to  CGHS for 2002-2003.  The Committee notes that Plan

allocation of Rs. 12.00 crores in 2001-02 had to be reduced to Rs. 9.00 crores at the RE stage.  Explaining the decrease,
the Department replied that the CGHS earlier had proposals for expansion of its services by opening more CGHS
dispensaries which involves  creation of new posts. Fresh proposals for creation of new posts  under CGHS can be
referred to the Department of Expenditure only after the recommendations contained in the SIU Report of November,
1999 are  fully implemented.  However, due to a stay on the recommendations contained in the SIU Report by CAT,
New Delhi, it was not possible for the CGHS to open more dispensaries by creation of new posts and this resulted in
less expenditure during the year 2001-2002. 
3.3       The Committee notes that it has not been possible to carry out the expansion programme of CGHS dispensaries
to new cities as was planned by the Ministry of Health during the Ninth Plan Period, due to the fact that the Ministry of
Finance had not agreed to the creation of new posts of setting up of new dispensaries  pending finalisation of the SIU
report on the functioning of CGHS dispensaries.  The Committee is deeply disturbed to note that provision of medical
facilities to the government employees which is a basic necessity  is trapped into avoidable legal wrangles.  The
Ministry should have taken up the matter with the Central Administrative Tribunal for early resolution of the case(s) so
that the expansion programme of dispensaries was implemented expeditiously.  The Committee, therefore, would like
the Ministry to look into this and submit a report to the Committee within a period of three months  of the action taken
and the present status of opening new CGHS dispensaries area-wise.
3.4       The Committee was apprised that in places where there are no Central Government-run hospitals, the facilities
provided for in-patient treatment to CGHS beneficiaries are woefully inadequate.  Very few beds are reserved for them. 
Consequently, the patients are put to avoidable inconvenience and have to seek treatment through private facilities
which are very expensive.  The Committee, therefore, would like the Ministry to look into this aspect and furnish details
of the facilities available to the CGHS beneficiaries in private-run hospitals for CGHS beneficiaries and measures taken
to augment the same.

IV.       SAFDARJUNG  HOSPITAL
4.1
              The Plan allocation for Safdarjung Hospital for the year 2002-2003 is Rs.42.00 crores against a   projected
demand  of  Rs.57.69 crores.   The Department has explained that out of Rs.42.00 crores allocated for Safdarjung
Hospital during the year 2002-2003, Rs. 37.50 crores are meant for Safdarjung Hospital and Rs. 4.50 crores are
allocated for the recently established college, i.e. Vardhman Mahavir Medical college (VMMC) at Safdarjung Hospital. 
Out of Rs. 37.50 crores provided for Safdarjung Hospital, only Rs. 10.30 crores are for procurement of machinery and
equipment and rest of the amount is meant  for meeting the salary/wages expenses of the staff and other routine
expenditure. 
4.2       The  Committee notes that the required faculty and infrastructure is being made available for the VMMC.   As
the  first session of the new college has already commenced, the Committee  urges upon the Department to take
concerted efforts to make the college fully functional at the earliest so that the students are not put to any problem. 
4.3       The issue of vacant posts in Safdarjung Hospital  has been engaging the attention of the Committee for quite
some time.  The Committee notes that out of total sanctioned strength of 4647, staff in position is 4120.   Latest position
as given by the Department is that the Screening Committee at its meeting held on 4.10.01 had recommended 22 posts
for filling up as per the guidelines of the Department of Personnel & Training O.M. dated 11.5.2001.  To fill up the
above 22 posts, N.O.C.  from Surplus cell has been obtained in January, 2002 and further action for  filling up these
posts is under process.  The whole exercise will be completed by the end of May, 2002.  The Medical Superintendent
has also been directed to undertake a comprehensive review of various posts lying vacant/likely to fall vacant and come
up with a proposal for filling up of additional posts within the overall ceiling prescribed by the Department of Personnel
& Training.  Besides, all out efforts are being made to fill up the other vacant posts by taking up the matter with
Ministry of Finance and other competent authorities on priority.
4.4       The Committee is of the view that procedural formalities should be expedited so that the 22 posts recommended
by the Screening Committee are filled at the earliest.   Besides that,  ongoing comprehensive review of various vacant
posts/likely to fall vacant by the Medical Supdt. Should not be unduly  delayed in procedural wrangles.  The Department
should also impress upon the Ministry of Finance the urgency for filling up the required posts of Safdarjung Hospital
which is the biggest Hospital in the capital catering to the needs of not only local patients but also from the 
neighbouring States.
4.5
              Given the unsatisfactory services being provided by the Safdarjung Hospital, the Committee in its earlier Report
recommended that the Department should resort to strict measures so that employees are made to carry out the duties
assigned to them.  The Department has replied that the employees of the hospital are constantly supervised and
controlled by their supervisors, so as to get the best out of them. Necessary disciplinary/administrative actions like
warning, deduction in salary are being taken against the erring staff.  The Department has also given a list of
disciplinary/administrative actions taken during the past three year against the erring staff .

with a provision of Rs. 10.00 lakhs every year for the remaining four years of the project period.   Thereafter, the district
project is taken over by the State.  As per the information made available to the Committee, about 20 States have been
released funds during the period from 1990-2002.   However, only Panchmahal district of Gujarat has been granted
three Grants – 1
st in 1990-91, 2nd in  1993-94 and 3 rd in 1996-97.   Besides  that, only three more districts  of Gujarat
have been released financial grants twice but not as per the prescribed guidelines.   Districts of  19 States have been
released funds only once.   Lack of utilization of earlier grants has been given as the main reason for such a dismal
situation.   The Committee observes that more than ten years have passed since the beginning of the Scheme and funds
are  simply being released without  any effort being made for ascertaining the  reasons for total lack of interest on the
part of State Govts.   The Committee  is of the view that drastic steps need to be taken for reviewing the Scheme for its
proper implementation.

          National Malaria Eradication Programme is a category II Centrally Sponsored Scheme on 50.50 Cost sharing
basis between the Centre and State Governments.  The Central Government on its part provides drugs, insecticides and
larvicides etc.  The State Governments meet the operational cost including salary of the staff, except North Eastern
States, which are being provided 100% Central assistance under the programme since December, 1994. 
12.2
          The Plan allocation for National Anti Malaria Programme in BE 2001-02 was Rs.168.00 crores which was
increased to Rs.173.00 crores at the RE stage.  Plan allocation for 2002-2003 has been further increased to Rs.187.00
crores, additional allocation meant for construction of two new buildings, one each for Directorate of the National Anti-
Malaria Programme and Malaria Research Centre under ICMR. 
12.3     The Committee observes that during the Ninth Plan, funds allocated for this Programme have invariably
remained under-utilised.  During 2000-01, BE allocation of Rs. 255.00 crores had to be reduced to Rs. 194.00 crores at
the RE stage and actual expenditure incurred was Rs. 188.32 crores.   Although BE allocation  of Rs. 168.00 crores in 
BE  2001-02 was enhanced to Rs. 173.00 crores at RE stage,  expenditure reported upto  February, 2002 is only
Rs.116.92 crores.  Seeing the trend in earlier years, the Committee is not inclined to  believe the Department’s
contention that the balance  amount  will be utilized during the remaining part of the financial year.

th September, 1997 for a period of

30.4.2001.  Low utilization of funds during the first year of the Project, non-appointment of Malaria-Link Volunteers

payment to MLVs from the project funds be met during the Project period.   Additional staff has also  been provided to

measures will increase the utilization of funds by the States.  The Committee would like to be apprised about the
utilization of funds by the State Governments in the year 2002-2003 which is the last year of the EMCP.

          The Committee notes that spray coverage during the year 2000 was around 60% in the states of Arunachal

D & N Haveli, Daman & Diu and Delhi. 174.83 million population were targeted to be covered by residual insecticidal
spray in 2000-01, but only 67 million population could be covered as per reports received upto September, 2001.

National TB Control Programme (RNTCP) based on WHO recommended  DOTs Strategy (Directly Observed
Treatment Short Course Chemotherapy) was launched in the country in March, 1997 with a soft loan from World
Bank.   Against the targeted coverage of 271.21 million population, under RNTCP  more than 430 million population
has already been covered.   The revised strategy is also being implemented in Andhra Pradesh and Orissa with the
assistance of DFID and DANIDA at a cost of  Rs. 109.93 crores and Rs. 31.95 crores respectively to cover a total
population of 100 million.
15.2     Plan Allocation under the T.B. Control Programme for BE 2001-2002 was Rs.122.00 crores which was
substantially reduced to Rs.100.00 crores at the RE stage. The Department has clarified that delay in the procurement of
anti-TB drugs to be supplied to various States/districts and non-procurement of binocular microscopes during the
financial year resulted in the reduction of funds meant for this purpose from Rs. 44.43 crores to Rs. 32.55 crores. 
Allocation  for grants to State/District TB Societies was also reduced from Rs. 56.00 crores to Rs. 42.50 crores.  Reason
being funds meant to be released to the new 120 districts under the expansion plan could not be fully released due to
delayed approval of the EFC and CCEA.   Surplus funds lying with some district societies was another reason for
reduction.   The Committee observes that this trend has been there during the entire Ninth Plan period.   As per the
figures  available with the Committee, out of plan allocation of Rs. 581.00 crores from 1997-98 to 2001-02, the total
expenditure incurred  as  on 22.2.02 is only Rs. 398.48 crores.   The Committee finds that achievement level of Physical
Targets  under Sputum Examination and Sputum Positive Detection has also  been much  below the fixed targets  during
the Ninth Plan period.
15.3     Last year, the Committee’s attention was drawn toward under-utilisation of funds released as Grants-in-aid- to
some State Govts. for procurement of anti-TB drugs for sputum negative cases.   The Committee apprehends that
situation may not have improved much.  The Committee is constrained to note Utilisation Certificates are  still awaited
from some State Govts. in spite of reminders.  Pending Utilisation Certificates, no further funds are being  released to
the State  Govt. for purchase of anti-TB drugs for sputum negative cases.  The Committee views this with serious

with all concerned State Govts.

           The Committee notes that five different schemes for  involvement of NGOs have been envisaged and NGOs are

implementing one project of involving private practitioners in E. Delhi and further expansion of this Project is

nd Phase of World Bank

the Govt. to the State Govts. and the nodal institutes to  meet the expenditure on staff, equipments, training, IEC

19.2  Against a  Plan allocation of Rs. 4.00 crores in RE 2001-02, allocation in BE 2002-2003 has been astronomically

based on the Tenth Five Year Plan proposal which envisages apart from sustaining the existing District Mental Health

existing mental health facilities in mental hospitals and psychiatric departments of medical colleges; to undertake
research in the field of mental health and to develop, disseminate and use   IEC programmes at national level.
19.3  The Committee notes that shortage of trained psychiatric manpower and lack of awareness regarding treatment are
the two main barriers to the provision of mental health services in the country.  The Committee has been given to
understand that about 4000 clinical psychologists,  psychiatric  social workers  and  psychiatric nurses are working in
the country which is inadequate to meet the total needs of  persons  with mental disorders in the country.  The shortage
of psychiatric manpower is felt in all the States, specially in rural areas.  The Committee strongly feels that there is a
need for having systematic evaluation regarding Statewise requirement of manpower.  The Committee also observes
that mental health programmes are being implemented in a varying degree by different States.   The Committee has
been informed that the District Mental Health Programme is to be enlarged and made more effective covering the  entire
country during the Tenth Plan.   The Committee feels that there  is an urgent need for expanding the mental health
services.  While  appreciating the substantive allocation of funds for this programme for 2002-03, the first year of Tenth
Plan, the Committee would like to emphasise that there should be regular and extensive monitoring at all levels to
ensure optimum and judicious utilization of funds.

 XX      PREVENTION  OF  FOOD  ADULTERATION  PROGRAMME
20.1  The subject of the Prevention of Food Adulteration is in the Concurrent list of the Constitution.  However, in
general, the enforcement of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is done by the State/UT. Governments.  The
Central Government primarily plays an advisory role in its implementation besides carrying out various statutory
functions/duties assigned to it under the various provisions of the Act.
20.2     Four Central Food Laboratories have been established under the Act, which work as appellate laboratories for
the purpose of analysis of samples of food lifted by the Food Inspectors of the States/U.Ts. and local bodies.  There are
82 Food Laboratories under the administrative control of various State/Union Territory Governments and Local Bodies.
20.3
             On being asked about experience of the Department in respect of administration of Prevention of Food
Adulteration Act and the Rules made thereunder, the Department has informed that some of the problems being faced
relate to inadequate enforcement at the level of the States.  There is a shortage of trained manpower, especially at the
level of food inspectors. Number of samples drawn for test and analysis has declined as also the cases in which
prosecutions have been launched or conviction obtained.  Capabilities of the State Food Laboratories are also required
to be augmented so that they can properly undertake analysis of contaminants.
20.4           The Department has also informed that the Government of India has been trying to assist the State Governments
by training of State Laboratory analysts and food inspectors and by supply of equipments to the laboratories.  The States
have been requested to increase their manpower for proper enforcement of the Act; to increase the budget to provide
proper facilities in the states laboratories and to utilize  the equipments provided by the Government of India properly;
to conduct investigational market surveys in a systematic way, with particular reference to items of mass consumption
and to keep a proper data bank of the results. 
20.5     From the feedback given by the Department, the Committee is left with no alternative but to believe that the
situation is indeed very grim so far as implementation of the   Prevention of Food Adulteration Act is concerned.   It
seems that with the load of so many Disease Control Programmes, this aspect of health management is  not getting the
due impetus from any State in the country.   The Committee is therefore, of the view that drastic measures are required
to be taken.   The Committee recommends that an overall review of Prevention of Food Adulteration Programme with
special focus on status of State laboratories, requirement of more labs and necessary staff therefor should be initiated
without any further delay.

of psychiatric manpower is felt in all the States, specially in rural areas.  The Committee strongly feels that there is a

that mental health programmes are being implemented in a varying degree by different States.   The Committee has
been informed that the District Mental Health Programme is to be enlarged and made more effective covering the  entire
country during the Tenth Plan.   The Committee feels that there  is an urgent need for expanding the mental health
services.  While  appreciating the substantive allocation of funds for this programme for 2002-03, the first year of Tenth
Plan, the Committee would like to emphasise that there should be regular and extensive monitoring at all levels to
ensure optimum and judicious utilization of funds.       (Para 19.3)
 XX      PREVENTION  OF  FOOD  ADULTERATION  PROGRAMME
From the feedback given by the Department, the Committee is left with no alternative but to believe that the
situation is indeed very grim so far as implementation of the   Prevention of Food Adulteration Act is concerned.   It
seems that with the load of so many Disease Control Programmes, this aspect of health management is  not getting the
due impetus from any State in the country.   The Committee is therefore, of the view that drastic measures are required
to be taken.   The Committee recommends that an overall review of Prevention of Food Adulteration Programme with
special focus on status of State laboratories, requirement of more labs and necessary staff therefor should be initiated
without any further delay.  (Para 20.5)
XXI        DEVELOPMENT OF NURSING SERVICE

116th Report

               The Committee feels that in a situation when large number of the people of this country particularly living in
remote and far flung areas are outside the reach of Health Care Delivery System, continuing with such a process which
makes the opening  of new Nursing Schools a long drawn one is not desirable.  The Committee, therefore, recommends
that appropriate steps should be taken so that avoidable procedural requirements are done away with.  The Committee
would also like to be apprised about the full details regarding Projects of Nursing Schools/colleges sanctioned and lying
pending (Statewise). (Para 21.2)
XXII    DRUGS  STANDARD CONTROL  PROGRAMME
               The Committee feels that the silence on the part of State Governments in furnishing the requite information is
perhaps due to their inability to  fill up the vacant posts.  The Committee views this very seriously and recommends that
the Department should pursue this matter relentlessly  with the State Governments. The Committee notes that there are
no drug testing laboratories in Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Pondicherry, Andaman & Nicobar
Islands, Chandidgarh, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Uttaranchal, Jharkhand and Chattisgarh.  Drug testing labs in States in
general except for the labs in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh fall below the required
levels.  The Committee finds that a countrywide auditing of all drug testing laboratories including Govt. testing
laboratories has been initiated.   The Committee welcomes this initiative  and hopes that this will result in proper
assessment of requirements in this vital sector and resultant follow-up action. (Para 22.3)
XXIII      HOSPITAL WASTE MANAGEMENT
On the perusal of the list, the Committee is shocked to find that  in respect of the States/UT  of Bihar, Manipur, 
Rajasthan and Chandigarh no action has been initiated by the State Pollution Control Boards or Pollution Control
Committees against the erring hospitals/nursing homes.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that this matter should
be taken up with the concerned Ministry, without any delay.  (Para 23.3)
XXIV   IMPLEMENTATION OF HEALTH PROGRAMMES IN  NORTH EAST SECTOR
Status of various National Health Programme in North-Eastern States is as follows :
NATIONAL PROGRAMME FOR CONTROL OF BLINDNESS:-
         The Committee observes  that Cataract Surgery performance rate  is low in all States except Tripura.   Assam is
one of the lowest performing States in the country with Cataract Surgery rate as low as 162 operations per lakh
population against the national rate of 400. (Para 24.2)
         The Committee notes that State Blindness Control Societies have been constituted so far in the States of
Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura only.   The Committee has been given to understand that eye care
infrastructure is weak in  NE region, particularly  in Assam.   Very few NGOs are located in the region.   Number of
Eye surgeons is also very inadequate.   The Committee feels that in spite of adequate funds  being provided, the
programme is not functioning well.   Non-setting up/non-functioning of District Blindness Control Societies and lack of
NGO involvement seem to be the two major handicaps.   The Committee recommends that the  Department should
vigorously  pursue  the implementation of the Programme with all the NE States. (Para 24.3)
The Committee apprehends that reason for the drastic cut in allocation of funds may be unspent balances lying
with the State Govts.   If that be so, it is  a cause of serious concern.   The Committee would like to be enlightened on
this aspect. (Para 24.8)
NATIONAL AIDS CONTROL PROGRAMME 
The Committee is shocked to find that not a single North-Eastern State has been able to fully utilize the funds
allocated to them and the States of Assam and Tripura failed to utilize even a single penny.  The Committee feels that
there is something seriously amiss in respect of these States and recommends that the Department should make an
enquiry into the matter.  (Para 24.10)

PREFACE
 
            I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource
Development, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this
Hundred-Seventeenth Report of the Committee on the Demands for Grants (Demand No.44) of the Department of
Family Welfare,  Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for the year 2002-2003.
 
2.         The Committee considered the various documents and relevant papers received from the Department of Family
Welfare and also heard the Secretary and other Officials of that Department   on the said Demands for Grants in its
meeting held on 28
th   March, 2002.
 
3.         The Committee considered the Draft Report and adopted the same in its meeting held on     24th  April, 2002.

Vaishakha 4,   1924 (Saka)

REPORT
I           INTRODUCTION
1.1       The Census of 2001 had indicated the population of India as 1027 million with 531 million males and 496
million females.    In the decade  1991-2001, nearly 181 million persons were added to the population of India.  
Population increased at an annual exponential growth rate of 1.93 percent in the decade.  As per the latest Sample
Registration System (SRS) estimates, the annual growth rate of population is 1.74% (1999).  
1.2       The eight States of U.P., Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Uttaranchal, Chhatisgarh and Orissa,
which currently constitute nearly 44% of the total population of India, are projected to comprise 48% of the total
population in 2016.   In other words, these States alone will contribute an anticipated 55% increase during the period
1996-2016.    Demographic outcome in these States will determine the timing and size of population at which India
achieves population stabilisation.
1.3       The three most significant factors that can curtail the growth of population are increase in the use of
contraceptives, improvement in the mother’s health and survival of children.  All the programmes of the Department of
Family Welfare are accordingly planned and being implemented for pursuing a combination of these three issues.
1.4       During the Tenth  Plan the main approach of family welfare programme will be:
(i)
                  To assess the needs for Reproductive and Child Health (RCH);
(ii)                To provide need based ,client centered and demand driven RCH care;
(iii)               To strengthen the infrastructure for service delivery and bridging the gap in essential infrastructure and
manpower;
(iv)              Providing additional assistance to poorly performing districts and ensuring uninterrupted supply of drugs
and equipments;  and

1.6       In respect of achievement of performance in Family Planning methods and to achieve the long term goals, the
following levels of contraceptives were achieved during 1996-97 to 2000-2001.

1.7       The Committee understands that under the Community Needs Assessment Approach (CNAA), an action plan is
prepared each year at the district level based  on the need assessment done by ANMs of Sub-Centre at village level.  In
the beginning of the financial year, the health worker will first complete the house-to-house survey.  Based on this
survey, Eligible Couple Register is updated by the ANM.  The Committee has been informed that the State Govts. are 
impressed from time to time to ensure that the Sub-Centre action is got prepared for each Sub-Centre in the State.  The
Committee has its own doubts about the implementation of this annual exercise, which is most essential for successful
implementation of Family Welfare Programme, specially in the remote and inaccessible areas.  The Committee strongly
feels that surprise inspections in the performing as well as non-performing districts by Central teams/dedicated
NGOs/Social Workers can bring out the ground reality.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department
should initiate such an exercise in 2002-2003.

II          BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
2.1              The Committee has been informed that allocation for the Department for  2002-2003 is Rs. 4953.83 crores
against Rs. 4232.38 crores in BE 2001-2002 which was  reduced to Rs. 3721.67 crores at RE stage.   This represents  an
increase of Rs. 721.55 crores over the previous year.
2.2
              Commenting on the allocation, the Department submitted that the Annual Plan proposal for the year 2002-2003
was Rs. 7590.56 crores.  However, an allocation of Rs 4953.83 crores was approved by the Planning Commission.  As a
result of cut in plan proposal, funding of the infrastructural units in the States will be the most affected.   Besides that, 
other schemes like contractual appointments under RCH Programme, adolescent health care, supply of Dai kits,
promoting institutional deliveries, civil works at Sub Centres, urban slum project and strengthening of primary health
care infrastructure, may also be curtailed.
2.3
              The Committee  has also been given to understand that during 2001-2002, a cut of 710.00 crores (plan) was
proposed by the Ministry of Finance on the basis of expenditure  incurred by the Department till October, 2001
(51.19%).   However,  subsequently an assurance was given by the Ministry of Finance that if 75% expenditure was
incurred by the Department by December, 2001, the cut made in the outlay will be restored.    However, despite meeting
the targetted expenditure and the representations made at the highest level, the cut of Rs. 710 crores was only reduced to
Rs. 510 crores.  
2.4              The Committee agrees in principle with the Department's contention of there being no case for resorting to a cut
of Rs. 700.00 crores at the RE stage in 2001-2002 by the Ministry of Finance.  The Committee also notes that total plan
allocation of Rs. 3700.00 crores in 2001-2002 is anticipated to be utilised. Actual expenditure figures are not available
at present.  The Committee, however observes that during 2000-2001, against a higher projected requirement, plan
allocation was Rs. 3500.00 crores which was reduced to Rs. 3200.00 crores at the RE stage.  Actual expenditure was
even less i.e. Rs. 3071.35 crores.  The Committee strongly feels that inview of much higher allocation of Rs. 4930.00
crores in 2002-2003, the Department should ensure that funds allocated under various schemes are utilised optimally
and strictly as per the action plan to strengthen its case of higher allocation.
III        RURAL FAMILY WELFARE SERVICES
3.1
              The Rural Family Welfare Centres were set up at all block level PHCs sanctioned upto 1.4.1980 to provide
Family Planning and MCH Services in rural areas.  There are 5435 such centres functioning in the Country.  Besides
that, to provide basic health and family welfare services to the rural population 1,37,311 Sub-Centres  are currently
functioning out of which 97,757 Sub-Centres were funded by the Department till now. 
3.2              The Committee was informed that a Consultative Committee consisting of the representatives of the Planning
Commission, Department of Expenditure, States of Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan was constituted by
the Department in 1998.   The Committee examined the SWAP proposal between Rural Family Welfare Centres and
Sub-Centres and strongly recommended that in view of the importance of the rural Sub-Centres for the Family Welfare
Programme, and as the Rural Family Welfare Centres have lost their original identity and have become part of primary
health centre complexes at the block level, the Department of Family Welfare should assume the responsibility of
funding all 1,37,311 existing Sub-Centres.   In exchange, for accepting this responsibility the States should take over the
financial liability of maintaining the Rural Family Welfare Centres  (RFWC) numbering 5435.
3.3       The Department  also informed that the main purpose of the SWAP is to streamline the system of financing the
Sub-Centres. As the Sub-Centres were established by Central Government and State Governments during different time
periods it is difficult to assess the impact of the programme run by the Department.   Therefore, there was a need to
bring all the Sub-Centres under one umbrella for effective monitoring of the programme.   The Planning Commission
insisted  that a consensus be developed among the States on the issue of swaping these responsibilities between the State
and Department of Family Welfare.     The Committee in its 101
st Report had also recommended that the issue needed
to be discussed with the States/UTs before any decision was taken in this regard.  The Committee, however, notes that a
decision has already been taken to implement the SWAP proposal from 1.4.2002.  Therefore there  is no proposal for
requirement of Funds for RFWCs in the Tenth Plan.  Accordingly, no allocation has been made in BE 2002-2003.
3.4       The Committee is surprised to note that a final decision has already been taken by the Department inspite of
there being no consensus on this issue among the States.  According to the Department itself, outcome of
implementation of SWAP proposal will be that some states will be in an advantageous position by saving the funds and

117th Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/117threport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:25]
some States in a disadvantageous position.  For example, as per the information made available to the Committee,
whereas additionalliability in the case of Chandigarh will be only Rs. 7 lakhs, for West Bengal it will be as high as Rs.
17.74 crores.  The Committee wonders about the fate of Rural Family Welfare Centres in view of no allocation being
made by the Department in BE 2002-2003.  The Committee would, therefore, like to emphasise that the issue of
compensating the affected states should be sorted out at the earliest.
3.5       The Committee is sympathetic to  grievance of some of the State Governments  who will be placed
disadvantageously as a result of the proposal.  The Committee recommends that the Department should vigorously
pursue its proposal with the Planning Commission for compensating the affected states.   The Department should make
concerted efforts to fix a rational basis for distribution of liabilities amongst the State Governments so that no injustice
is done to any State.
3.6       The Committee notes that 22842 Primary Health Centres exist  in the country against the requirement of 25907
Primary Health Centres . However, there are only 5435 Rural Family Welfare Centres at present.   Hence, there is  a
need to open many more Rural Family Welfare Centres by the States.   Given the tight financial position of the State
Governments, the Committee feels that it is a great challenge for them. 
3.7       The Plan allocation for Sub-Centres for BE 2001-2002 was Rs. 675.00 crores which has been substantially
increased to Rs. 1909.00 crores in 2002-2003.   Commenting on the increase, the Department has informed that on
account of transfer of liability of 39,554 additional Sub-Centres, the requirement of the additional funds on this account
is Rs. 593 crores.   Adjustment of the funds according to SWAP proposal for Rural Family Welfare Centres now to be
funded by State Governments is Rs. 430 crore.  Thus an extra liability of Rs. 163 crores is to be borne by Central
Government.  Other  reasons for increase in BE 2002-2003 against BE/RE  2001-2002 are as follows:
(a)
     Revision of financial norms for pattern of assistance to States/UTs for Sub-Centre Scheme.
(b)    Increased salaries of staff of Sub-Centres in States/UTs following 5 th Central Pay Commission
recommendations.
(c)     Provision for payment of arrears to the State Governments of previous years which until now were being
provided from the scheme named Arrears.
3.8       The Department has informed that 137311 Sub Centres have been established against a requirement of 155455
Sub Centres as per 2002 projected population.   In Tribal areas, 21335 Sub Centres have been established against a
requirement of 26243 Sub Centres.   There are 22842   Primary Health Centres in the country against the requirement of
25907 PHCs and 3043 Community Health Centres against the requirement of 6479 CHCs, based on 2002 Projected
Population.
3.9       The number of Sub-Centres, PHCs and  CHCs required and shortfall as per 2002 projected population is given
below.

VII       POST PARTUM PROGRAMME
Post Partum Programme is a maternity centered hospital based approach to Family Welfare Programme covering
550 Post Partum Centres at district level and 1012 Post Partum Centres at sub-district level hospitals.   The objective of
the programme is to provide antenatal,  natal and post-natal services to expectant mothers and also to provide Family
Planning Services, besides diagnosing early cases of cervical cancer.   An allocation of  Rs 135.00 crores was made for
Post Partum Programme in BE 2001-2002.   However, no allocation has been made for the year 2002-2003.   Giving
reasons, the Department has replied that the Planning Commission has decided to transfer the Post Partum Programme
to the States/UTs w.e.f. 1.4.2002.  The Committee would be interested to know as to the precise reasons that weighed in
favour of transfer of this Programme to the States/UTs.

8.1
              Allocation of Rs. 117.00 crores made under the head Free Distribution of Conventional Contraceptive in BE
2001-2002 has been increased to Rs. 181.80 crores in 2002-2003.  Explaining the reasons for increase,  the Department
has informed that due to increasing number of younger couples, the demand for condoms under free distribution from
the States has been increasing and   in order to meet the enhanced demand, increased budgetary provision has been
proposed.
8.2       The Department has further informed that as regards allocation of additional quantities of conventional
contraceptives in the States, these would be allocated proportionately in relation  to utilisation and demand of the
respective States.   The unmet need in condom under free supply scheme is nearly 30% whereas in Oral Contraceptive
Pill (OCP) it is around 10%.   Attempts will be made to fill up these gaps.   The additional allocation would be required
for the purchase of the raw material for OCP which is no more available under external assistance and the same has to
be met from domestic resources.
8.3       In regard to the quality of Nirodh, the Committee has been given to understand that  19% users have rated it
under free supply scheme as okay,  75% as good and 6% have rated as very good.    The Committee feels that the
quality of condoms goes a long way in its acceptance by the users.    The Committee is also of the view that poor quality
may lead to unwanted pregnancy and reproductive tract infections.    The Committee,  therefore, recommends that the
Department should ensure that only the best quality of latex is used in manufacturing of condoms.

to rural people and therefore recommends that the Department should make concerted efforts to get  the posts of ANMs
and LHVs  filled up at the earliest in respect of the weak performing states.  (Para 3.16)
IV        URBAN FAMILY WELFARE SERVICES

The Committee is of the view  that for improving outreach service delivery system in urban slums,
reorganisation of Urban Family Welfare Centres should be made at the earliest.    Therefore, the Committee
recommends that the Department should make adequate provision for reorganisation of Urban Family Welfare Centres
in 2002-2003. (Para 4.4)
V         REPRODUCTIVE AND CHILD HEALTH PROGRAMME (RCH)
The Committee notes with appreciation the rationalization done by the Department in restructuring the RCH
Programme and feels that the Department should, in the same vein carry similar rationalization/ restructuring,  
wherever possible, in respect of other programmes.     (Para 5.3)
The Committee feels that the underutilization of funds  by the State governments is quite alarming  as it reflects
that the Programme is not being implemented properly at the ground level. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
the Department should take up the matter with the concerned  States and try to find out the reasons behind under
utilization of funds by them and take necessary remedial measures. (Para 5.4)
The Committee expresses its dissatisfaction that the Department has not so far taken up the matter with the State
Govts even after almost a year has passed.   It desires that this may be done at the earliest and the outcome may be
intimated to it. (Para 5.5)
            Noting the efforts made by the Department, the Committee feels that though some progress has been made in
respect of Infant mortality rate, percentage of safe delivery etc.,   they are still very high in comparison to even a
number  of developing countries.   Some States like Assam, Bihar, M.P., U.P., Orissa and Rajasthan continue to perform
much below the National Average.   In view of this, the Committee recommends  that the Department should make
extra efforts to improve the performance in these states. (Para 5.8)
The Committee feels that the Department should approach the concerned States for bringing out the necessary
improvements/modifications in the schemes for a better implementation of the same. (Para 5.9)
The Committee recommends that the Department should pursue with the remaining States also.  Efforts should
also be made to extend this scheme to more districts. (Para 5.10)
VI        STRENGTHENING OF IMMUNISATION PROGRAMME AND ERADICATION OF POLIO
            The Committee is deeply anguished to find that a cut in the allocation at the RE stage was made due to delay in
procurement of equipment and stores.    The Committee feels that such delays seriously affect the implementation of
Family WelfareProgrammes.  It,  therefore, recommends that the  Department should inquire into as to whether this
delay could have been avoided and if so, the responsibility should be fixed in this regard.  It should also take extra
precaution so that such delays are avoided in future.  (Para 6.2)
In case of BCG vaccination and DPT Immunization the Committee is happy to note that the all India
achievement is more than 100%.  However, again Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland are the low-performing
States.   The same can be said about DPT Immunisation coverage.    (Para 6.3)
             The Committee observes that the States like Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya  and Nagaland continue to
perform much  below the national average over the years in all the immunization programmes.  Another disturbing
feature noticed by the Committee  is the downward trend in the percentage of coverage during the last three years of
Ninth Plan in respect of some States.  The Committee therefore, recommends that the Department should identify such
States as are performing below the national average and take special steps to strengthen the immunization scheme in
such States.  (Para 6.4)
VII       POST PARTUM PROGRAMME
The Committee would be interested to know as to the precise reasons that weighed in favour of transfer of this
Programme to the States/UTs.
VIII      DISTRIBUTION OF CONTRACEPTIVES
            In regard to the quality of Nirodh, the Committee has been given to understand that  19% users have rated it
under free supply scheme as okay,  75% as good and 6% have rated as very good.    The Committee feels that the
quality of condoms goes a long way in its acceptance by the users.    The Committee is also of the view that poor quality
