 REPORT
I           INTRODUCTION
1.1       The Department of Women and Child Development was set up in 1985 as a part of the Ministry of Human
Resource Development to give the much needed impetus to the  holistic development of women and children.
1.2       In its capacity as a nodal agency looking after the advancement of women and children, the Department 
formulates plans, policies and programmes, enacts and amends legislation affecting women and children and guides and
coordinates the efforts of both governmental and non-governmental organizations working in the field of women and
child development.   Apart from this, the Department implements certain innovative programmes for women and
children which are in the areas of training and capacity building, employment and income generation, welfare and
support services, awareness generation and gender sensitization. 
II
          PERFORMANCE DURING NINTH PLAN
2.1       Approved outlay during the Ninth  Plan for the Department  was Rs. 7810.42 crores.   Allocation of Rs. 900.00
crores in the first year of the Plan (1997-98) showed an upward trend with Rs. 1650.00 crores being provided in 2001-
02 which was the   last year  of Ninth Plan.   With the exception of first year, the Committee observes  that the
Department failed to utilize the allocated funds fully.  There was invariable reduction at the RE stage and that too
sometimes remained under-utilised.   The main factors responsible for this trend which were noticed by the Committee
were non-performance of implementing agencies, be it State Govts or NGOs, unspent balances lying with them, non-
submission of Utilisation Certificates, non-receipt of viable proposals, release of funds in the last quarter of financial
year etc. 
2.2       The Committee is constrained to note that as compared to children-related schemes, women-related schemes
need special focusing.  Although amount of funding for women-related schemes is much less, the same remained
grossly under-utilised during the entire Ninth Plan period.   So far as  achievement level  of physical targets for different
schemes relating to both women and children is concerned, the Committee is surprised to note that they remained more
or less fulfilled, in some schemes, achievement  level is exceeding the targets fixed.   This is despite the fact that trend
of under-utilisation of funds was noticed with respect to women-related schemes.   The Committee apprehends that
there is  likelihood of over-achievement of physical targets being on paper only,   ground reality being  totally
different.   The Committee also feels that there might be  a possibility of physical targets being fixed without proper
assessment.   The Committee is of the view that in either case, an effective inbuilt monitoring mechanism at all required
levels can reveal the real picture.

2002-03 against Rs. 1650.00 crores allocated in BE and RE 2001-02, representing an increase of Rs. 550.00 crores.

IV        INTEGRATED CHILD DEVELOPMENT SERVICES (ICDS)
4.1       The ICDS Scheme seeks to provide an integrated package of health, nutrition and educational services to
children up to six years of age, pregnant women and nursing mothers.   The package includes supplementary nutrition,
immunization, health check-up, referral services, nutrition and health education and non-formal pre-school education.  
Number of sanctioned ICDS Projects is 5652 including 922 World Bank assisted Projects.  Out of these, 4587 Projects
including 752 World Bank assisted Projects are operational as on 31.12.01.    The Scheme is a centrally sponsored
Scheme.  While the Central Govt. bears the full cost of meeting the operational requirements, the States  provide for
funds for supplementary nutrition component.

VI        TRAINING PROGRAMME UNDER ICDS (UDISHA)
6.1       Training is a crucial element in the ICDS Scheme.  ‘UDISHA’ is a comprehensive training programme being
undertaken through the National Institute of Public Co-operation and Child Development, selected training  institutions,
and the State Govts.   World Bank assistance is available for  part of the expenditure for this programme.  The
functionaries trained in the programme include the Anganwadi Workers, Supervisors, Additional Child Development
Project Officers (ACDPOs), Child Development Project Officers (CDPOs), Medical Officers and para-medical staff.  
UDISHA has an outlay of Rs. 600.55 crores over a  five-year period from 1999-2000 to September, 2004.
6.2       The Budget allocation in BE 2001-02 was Rs. 40.00 crores which was enhanced to Rs. 55.00 crores at RE
stage.   Provision of Rs. 72.00 crores has been made for BE 2002-03.   The Committee notes that during 2001-02, as
against the total release of  Rs. 36.15 crores (till 28.2.02),  the expenditure reported by the States/UTs and the NIPCCD
is Rs. 26.00 crores (upto December, 2001). 
6.3       The Committee has been given to understand that the training facilities are now better organized at  the State/UT
level and the  various training activities are being taken up in a big way in order to clear the training backlog during the
project period.  The Committee is, however, not inclined to agree with the contention of the Department.  The 
Committee observes that upto 31.12.01, against a target of training of 605 CDPOs, only 252 CDPOs have been trained.  
Similarly, out of 3428 Supervisors to be trained, only 1199 Supervisors have been imparted training. 
6.4       The  Committee finds that against a total release of Rs. 109.56 crores upto 25.2.02, total expenditure incurred by
States/UTs is Rs. 97.60 crores  and Statements of Expenditure received amount to Rs. 88.30 crores.   States/UTs of
Jharkhand, Uttaranchal, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu and Lakshdweep have
failed to furnish  the SOEs in spite of repeated requests.   States of Assam, Goa, Gujarat, Manipur, Nagaland, Sikkim
and Tamil Nadu are lagging behind in submission of SOEs.   The Committee is perturbed to note that against total
release of Rs. 413.41 lakhs to Tamil Nadu, expenditure figures are Rs. 205.92 lakhs and total SOEs  received are only
for Rs. 57.94 lakhs.   Not only majority of States have failed to utilize fully funds allocated to them, pendency is there in
respect of submission of expenditure details too.   The Committee strongly feels that a midterm review of this Training
Project should be undertaken without any delay so that assessment about the constraints/shortcomings  can be
made.

institutions have been  requested to send the necessary papers for making payments.   The Committee, however, notes
that upto 28.2.02, an expenditure of only Rs. 9.07 crores has been incurred.   The Committee is not in favour of release
of funds during the last month of the financial year.   The Committee, therefore, recommends that necessary  measures
should be taken for expeditious disposal of proposals. 
10.3     The Committee observes that during the Ninth Plan overall performance so far as achievement level of Physical
and financial targets is  concerned has been satisfactory.  The Committee, however, feels that the Scheme is being
implemented by only ten to twelve States as  is evident from the details of funds released during the years 1998-99,
1999-2000 and 2000-01.  The Committee feels that efforts should be made to expand the Scheme to the uncovered
States also.   The Committee, therefore, recommends that required steps in this direction should be taken.   The
Committee is not aware   whether any exercise of evaluating the  Scheme has been undertaken so far.   If not, the

XII       HOSTELS FOR WORKING WOMEN
12.1     The Scheme aims to provide suitable and economical accommodation to working women whose income does
not exceed Rs. 16,000/- p.m. in ‘A’ class cities and Rs. 15,000/- p.m. in other cities.           Financial assistance is given
to the extent of 75% of the cost of construction of the hostel building and 50%  of the cost of the land by the Centre to
eligible voluntary organizations, universities, public trusts etc.    States/UTs are also eligible for assistance if suitable
organizations are not available in the area.
12.2     Allocation  of Rs. 9.00 crores in BE 2001-02 was reduced to Rs. 7.00 crores at RE stage and expenditure
reported upto 28
th February, 2002 is only Rs. 4.04 crores.   The Committee  observes that enhanced allocation in BE
2001-02 was meant for expenditure on claims for 2 nd instalment  for 29 Working Hostels sanctioned in 2000-01 and
third and final instalment of several hostels sanctioned in previous years.   However, due to anticipated  claims not
forthcoming, allocation had to be reduced at the RE stage.   The Committee finds that an allocation of Rs. 13.50 crores
has been made for 2002-03 in order to cover the requirement of women seeking employment, expansion of the Scheme
and revision of norms proposed to be undertaken during the year.   The Committee does not have  much faith in  these
proposed plans in view of working of the Scheme during Ninth Plan.  Utilization of funds under the Scheme has been
optimum during the Ninth Plan with the exception of last year, 2001-02.     However, the same cannot be said about the
achievement  level of physical targets during Ninth Plan.   Although 87 hostels have been sanctioned against the  target
of 93  hostels, the Committee apprehends that very few would have been constructed and made operational.   This is 
borne out by the fact that achievement level with regard to number of beneficiaries is much below the targeted figures.
12.3     The Committee observes that  State/UTs are being requested to provide status position with regard to sanctioned
hostels at regular intervals.   Last reminder has been sent on 11.10.2001 whereby all Chief Secretaries/Women and
Child Development Secretaries were asked to provide list of incomplete hostels.   District Collectors  and CDPOs were 
also requested to conduct inspections and furnish reports.  The Committee is constrained to note that all this exercise has
failed to achieve any results.   Information giving very little details has been received only from the States of Rajasthan,
J&K, Chattisgarh, Mizoram and Bihar.   The Committee is, therefore, of the opinion that sanction for construction of
new hostels should not be given at any cost.   Instead all attention should be diverted to get the construction of all
pending hostels completed at the earliest within a prescribed and closely monitored time schedule.   The Committee
would also like to be  enlightened about the number of  Hostels sanctioned, under construction and operational hostels
(State-wise).   The Committee strongly feels that there is an urgent need for conducting an  evaluation of this Scheme so
as to assess  the inherent drawbacks and suggest necessary modifications therefor.
12.4     The Committee would like to point out that there have been instances when needy and eligible women  are
deprived accommodation in the hostels. Instead those women who are not entitled for such a facility  continue to occupy
the hostels beyond the prescribed time limit.   The Committee feels that there is a need for strict implementation of the 
guidelines prescribed under the Scheme so that such instances do not occur.

very little details has been received only from the States of Rajasthan, J&K, Chattisgarh, Mizoram and Bihar.   The
Committee is, therefore, of the opinion that sanction for construction of new hostels should not be given at any cost.  
Instead all attention should be diverted to get the construction of all pending hostels completed at the earliest within a
prescribed and closely monitored time schedule.   The Committee would also like to be  enlightened about the number
of  Hostels sanctioned, under construction and operational hostels (State-wise).   The Committee strongly feels that there

is an urgent need for conducting an  evaluation of this Scheme so as to assess  the inherent drawbacks and suggest
necessary modifications therefor. (Para 12.3)
The Committee feels that there is a need for strict implementation of the  guidelines prescribed under the
Scheme so that such instances do not occur.   (Para 12.4)
XIII      SHORT STAY HOMES
            The Committee, however, observes that against an allocation of Rs. 10.00 crores in 2001-02, expenditure
reported upto 28.2.02 is only Rs. 5.32 crores.   Overall performance of the Scheme during Ninth Plan cannot be
considered to be satisfactory.   Due to unspent balances available with the  implementing agencies,  the trend of
reduction of funds at RE stage and that too remaining underutilized has been observed .   The Committee feels that
maintenance and supervision of the existing SSHs being handed over to CSWB in 1999-2000 has not led to any
noticeable improvement.  (Para 13.3)
            The Committee notes that  as on 8.3.02  there are 374 Short Stay Homes spread over in 26 States/UTs  with the
maximum number concentrated in AP, Bihar, Orissa, UP and W. Bengal.  The Committee would like to be apprised
about the number of fully functional SSHs (state-wise) and also about the feedback received in respect of functioning of
above-mentioned States during 2001-02 as a result of inspections conducted by the Department Officials. (Para 13.4)
XIV     CENTRAL SOCIAL WELFARE BOARD (CSWB)
            The Committee notes that in some cases CSWB expenditure has exceeded the amount provided by the
Department during 2001-02.    In some schemes, although no funds have been provided by the Department, Board has
shown expenditure thereunder.   In some other cases, the Board has some amount as opening balance at the beginning of
the financial year.   It seems that the  Board was having unspent balance with it.  The Committee would like to be
enlightened in this regard. (Para 14.2)
The Committee strongly feels that   serious efforts should be made   for bringing out  improvement in the
functioning of CSWB.   (Para 14.3)
XV       NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR WOMEN
The Committee finds that sexual harassment complaints whenever referred to the Commission are sent to the
concerned organizations and their disposal  is monitored by the Commission.   The Committee would like to be
enlightened as to whether the Commission has initiated any exercise for ascertaining the compliance of aforesaid SC
judgement regarding setting up of complaint mechanism in all workplaces so far. (Para 15.2)
The Committee, however, feels that this is not the  ideal position and the concerned States/UTs should be
approached once again for setting up  Women Commissions. (Para 15.3)
XVI     NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR CHILDREN
The Committee notes that the proposed National Commission for Children is to  monitor all the schemes
pertaining to children at present being handled by different Departments.   This would facilitate the handling of  all the
children related problems in a holistic manner.    (Para 16.1)
XVII    RASHTRIYA MAHILA KOSH
            The issue of augmenting the corpus of RMK had been going  on for considerable time.  The Committee is happy
to note that EFC had finally recommended augmenting  RMK’s corpus fund to Rs. 100.00 crores with the year wise
scheduling of the disbursement to be need-based.   The Department has informed that RMK’s initial corpus of Rs. 31.00
crores already stands augmented to Rs. 52.06 crores.   Accordingly Rs. 47.94 crores   is the additionality to be provided
as a consequence of the EFC decision.   The Committee, however, observes  that the year-wise scheduling is yet to be
finalized and EFC recommendations are under process of sanction.   The Committee hopes that all the procedural
formalities will be expedited for augmenting the corpus fund of RMK. (Para 17.2)

            I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource
Development, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this 
Hundred –Twenty Second Report of the Committee on the Demands for Grants (Demand No.88) of the Ministry of
Youth Affairs and Sports for  the year 2002-2003.
2.         The Committee considered the various documents and relevant papers received from the Ministry of Youth
Affairs and Sports  and also heard the Secretary and other Officials of that Ministry on the said Demands for Grants in
its meeting held on 27
th   March, 2002.

REPORT
I           INTRODUCTION
1.1       The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports was initially set up as the Department of Sports in 1982 at the time of
organisation of the IX Asian Games in New Delhi.   Thereafter, during the celebration of the International Youth Year
in 1985, the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports came into being.  It became a Ministry on the 27
th May, 2000.
1.2       The Youth i.e. those falling within the age group of 15-35 years constitutes nearly 40% of the total population of
the country.   To optimally tap the constructive and creative energies of this most valuable human resource, the Ministry
of Youth affairs and Sports has taken a number of new initiatives since its inception.    The Ministry organises a large
number of programmes in the field of youth development,  sports and physical education.
1.3       The Secretary, while deposing before the Committee, highlighted the various activities undertaken by the

122nd Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/122ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:28]
Ministry during the year 2001-2002.   A mention was made about the celebration of the International Year of Volunteers
and the 7th National Youth Festival at Hissar.    Committee's attention was drawn to the initiative taken in the setting up
of a six- member National Commission for Youth.   The Secretary also informed that a new National Sports Policy has
been approved by the Government on the 11 th September, 2001.    The Committee was given to understand that as a
result of detailed review of all the youth related schemes, action was initiated for merger of some overlapping
schemes.    Similarly, a decision was taken to merge all the sports related schemes under six umbrella schemes.    The
Secretary apprised the Committee about two new Plan Schemes relating to State Sports Academy and Dope Test,
proposed to be started during the Tenth Plan.
II.         BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
2.1       The total outlay, both Plan and Non-Plan taken together provided to the Ministry for the year 2001-2002 was Rs.
315.00 crores which was marginally enhanced to Rs. 322.14 crores in RE 2001-2002.   The allocation made for 2002-
2003 is Rs. 339.39 crores (Plan Rs. 285.00 crores and Non Plan Rs. 54.39 crores).
2.2       Expressing its dissatisfaction with the enhanced allocation under Plan in 2002-2003, the Ministry clarified that
this increase would only enable it to implement the ongoing schemes better as per the present norms.  Against a
projected demand of Rs. 327.54 crores under Plan for the year 2002-2003  a provision of only Rs. 285.00 crores has
been made.   The projections were made, taking into consideration, higher requirements for  the new schemes to be
implemented by the Ministry during 2002-2003.
2.3       The Committee is aware that under the Constitution, Sports is a State subject and in the implementation of the
different youth and Sports related schemes, State Govts./ autonomous organisations/NGOs have to play a very active
role.    However, the Committee has observed that during the Ninth Plan period,  although the allocation has been
generally  less than the projected requirements, allocated funds after being reduced at the RE stage remained under-
utilised.   Another disturbing trend noticed by the Committee was non-uniform spread of expenditure during the year.  
Last year, the Committee had pointed out that the expenditure on different schemes should be planned in such a way
that last moment spending is avoided.   The Committee is, however, constrained to point out that the situation seems to
have worsened in 2001-2002.   Against a Plan allocation of Rs. 255.00 crore, expenditure reported as on 1.3.2002 is
only Rs. 155.84 crores.   Specially under  the Youth Welfare Schemes, expenditure reported upto 1.3.2002 is less than
half of the allocated funds (Plan allocation - Rs. 91.25 crores Exp. upto 1.3.2002 is Rs. 42.47 crores).    The Committee
strongly feels that the formulation of a quarterly annual action plan for 2001-2002 has failed to achieve the  desired
results.    The Committee would like to point out that instead of projecting higher requirements and launching new
schemes without completing the requisite formalities, focus should be on the judicious and optimum utilisation of funds
allocated for various schemes.   The Committee is of the view that a detailed review of all the ongoing schemes should
be undertaken so as to assess the shortcomings being noticed and take remedial steps for removal of the same.   The
Department should endeavour to involve the State Govts. and various implementing agencies in this exercise.
III.       NEHRU YUVA KENDRA SANGATHAN
3.1       Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS),  an autonomous organization of the Ministry,   has its network in 500
districts of the country.   It is one of the largest grass-root level organisations in the world, catering to the needs of more
than eight million non-student rural youth enrolled through 1.89 lakh village based Youth Clubs.     Every district of
NYK has a trained cadre of District Youth Coordinator, National Service Volunteers and Youth Leaders.   NYKS
accomplishes its task through two categories of Programmes  i.e. Regular Programmes such as Youth Club
Development, Vocational Training, Work Camp, Awareness Generation, Cultural Programme, Sports Promotion etc.
and Seminars and Workshops and Celebration of National and International Days/ Weeks and Schemes assigned to it by
the Ministry for Implementation.
3.2       During the period ending December 31, 2001, 856 Youth Club Development Programmes, 905 Awareness
Generation Programmes, 2005 Vocational Training Programmes, 1875 tournaments for sports promotion, 444
workshops and seminars, 796 cultural programmes were organised and 4025 National days/weeks were celebrated.  
Besides that, Nehru Yuva Kendras of 13 districts (10 from U.P. and 3 from West Bengal), having  polio incidence,
conducted  extensive awareness campaigns in all blocks of these districts.    The Committee also notes that positive
response has been received to the Swarnjyanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana launched in November, 2000 in 8 districts of
Assam, Jharkhand, Bihar, Orissa, M.P. and Chattisgarh with the financial support from the Ministry of Rural
Development.   A proposal to expand the project in six more districts is at present under the consideration of the

122nd Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/122ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:28]
Ministry of Rural  Development.
3.3       An allocation of Rs. 28.38 crores has been made for NYKS under Plan in BE 2002-2003 against a provision of
Rs. 23.23 crores in BE 2001-2002.   On a specific query about the reasons for enhanced allocation in the current year, it
has been informed that the hike of Rs.5.15 crores in Plan allocation was due to construction of an office-cum-training
complex at a satellite town of Delhi on land owned by the Sangathan and to meet the committed liability  of increase in
the salaries of the staff due to annual increment, DA etc.
3.4       The Committee, however, notes that an expenditure of only Rs. 11.12 crores has been incurred upto 1.3.2002
against an allocation of Rs. 23.23 crores in BE 2001-2002.   The Committee has been given to understand that during
2000-2001, the last instalment  of GIA  was released to NYKS only in the last week of March, 2001 as the Utilisation
Certificate submitted by the Sangathan was not in an appropriate  format.   The Committee  apprehends that non-
submission of Utilisation Certificate and statement of  accounts within  the prescribed time limit must be one of the
reasons for expenditure of only one-third of the allocated funds under NYKS during 2001-2002.   The Committee would
like to be apprised about the factors responsible for such a discouraging trend.  
3.5       Annual Report for the year 2001-2002  highlights a variety of regular programmes like Youth Club
Development,  Awareness Generation, Vocational Training etc.    organised and seminars and workshops conducted by
various Nehru Yuva Kendras and on each programme/workshop etc.   funds ranging from Rs. 4,000 to Rs. 30,000 per
Kendra have been either allocated or earmarked.  The number of these programme/workshops must have increased by
the year end i.e. 31
st March, 2002.    The Committee strongly feels that either these achievements in majority of the
cases are on paper only or unspent balances are lying with  many Nehru Yuva Kendras.  Either way, it cannot be
considered an ideal position.    The Committee is of the view that the Department should not entirely depend on the
progress reports forwarded by the NYKS.   An effective  monitoring  mechanism  with an element of surprise 
inspections should be evolved.    It is understood that instructions have already been issued for associating the local
MPs/MLAs with the District Advisory Committee on Youth Programmes.    The Committee would like to be informed
within  a period of three months about the implementation of these instructions together with the details of the inter-
action with local MPs/MLAs. 
3.6       The Committee notes that a total of 492 district NYKs have District Advisory Committee for Youth Programme
(DACYPs) and for the remaining 8 districts, DACYPs are likely to be formed by the first quarter of 2002-2003.    The
Committee observes that against the prescribed 30% representation of women in DACYPs, national average comes to
36.47%.    The Committee is, however, constrained to point out that in some of the States/UTs, representation of
women  in DACYPs is much below the prescribed 30% .   For example in Lakshdweep, it is as low as 11.1% and in
West Bengal only 13.63%.    The Committee recommends that NYKS in such States/UTs. should be approached for
doing the needful in this regard.
3.7       The Committee has been given to understand that a number of initiatives have been taken during 2001-2002 to
give wide publicity to all the youth programmes undertaken by NYKS.    The Committee hopes that these efforts would
have the desired results.
IV        NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME (NSS)
4.1       The main objective of the National Service Scheme is development of the personality of students through
community service.   The scheme is being implemented through universities, colleges and +2 level schools and
institutions of higher learning in all the States/UTs.   At present, NSS has over 17 lakh student volunteers spread over
176 Universities and 16 Senior Secondary schools.   From its inception, more than 1.52 crore students from
Universities, colleges and Institutions of higher learning have benefited from NSS activities.
4.2       The expenditure on NSS programme is shared between the Central and the State Governments in the ratio of 7:5
except in the case of Jammu and Kashmir and Union Territories without legislatures, North-Eastern States including
Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh and other hilly areas as notified by the Planning Commission.   The sharing of expenditure in
such States/UTs  is 3:1.  The Central Government also meets the entire expenditure on administration, training, research,
monitoring, evaluation and publications pertaining to the scheme and full cost of NSS State Liaison Cells set up in the
concerned Department of State Governments.   The existing pattern of expenditure on NSS `Regular Activities' and
`Special Camping Activities' is Rs. 160 and Rs. 300 per volunteer per annum respectively except for North-Eastern
States & Hilly Terrain /Areas including Sikkim and Himachal Pradesh for which the pattern of expenditure is Rs. 200
and Rs.400 respectively.

122nd Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/122ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:28]
4.3       The Committee has been informed that due to proposed increase in the strength of NSS volunteers from 17:56
lakhs in 2001-2002 to 19.30 lakhs in 2002-2003, the Department had projected a demand of Rs. 39.91 crores for BE
2002-2003.   However, due to unspent NSS funds available with many State Govts/UTs, an allocation of only Rs. 23.40
crores has been provided in 2002-2003.   The Committee would like to point out that although allocation of funds might
have been less than the projected requirements of the Department in 1999-2000 and 2000-2001, allocated funds had
remained under-utilised.   Situation seems to have worsened in 2001-2002.   Against allocation of Rs. 23.85 crores, only
Rs. 9.15 crores have been utilised upto 1.3.2002.
4.4       While examining the Demands for Grants for 2000-2001, the Committee had expressed its serious concern over
non-settlement of accounts by a large number of States/UTs.  The Committee notes that since then, situation has
improved somewhat in respect of States like Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Mizoram, West Bengal,
Arunachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Chandigarh, Sikkim and Rajasthan.   However, in respect of the following
States, no improvement whatsoever has been made:

The Committee observes that situation might have improved in respect of some States/UTs, but the fact remains
that pendency in settlement  of accounts is there more or less in respect of all States/UTs.   The Committee expresses its
serious concern over this state of affairs specially in the case of above-mentioned States/UTs.   What is more shocking is
that implementing agencies under NSS are universities, colleges and +2 level schools and institutions of higher learning
and not NGOs lacking the required background.    The Committee finds it rather amazing that the Department has failed
to pursue the matter even with NCT of Delhi. 
4.5       The Committee is constrained to note that unspent NSS Grants amounting to Rs. 25,12,84,195 are lying with
various State Govts./UTs  with Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Punjab, Rajasthan, UP, Gujarat and Maharashtra
being the major defaulters. As per the accounting procedure under NSS, funds are transferred from Central Govt. to
State Govts.   The State  Govts. after adding their  share of funds transfer this amount to the Universities/+2 level
schools which, in turn, transfer this amount to the NSS implementing units in colleges/schools.   The States/UTs submit
their accounts in the prescribed proforma indicating the details of central share and matching state share grants.   The
Committee has been informed that the present accounting procedure is working satisfactorily and there was no proposal
to revamp it.   The Committee is, however, not inclined to agree with the contention of the Ministry.   Had it been so,
huge amount of unspent NSS Grants would not have been lying with many States/UTs.   The Committee is of the firm
view that there is an urgent need to review the accounting procedure under NSS and the Department should initiate
action in this regard.
V         NATIONAL SERVICE VOLUNTEER SCHEME
5.1       The objective of the scheme is to provide opportunities to students, generally speaking, those who have
completed their graduation to involve themselves, on a voluntary basis, in nation - building activities for a specific
period on a whole time basis.   Any person who has completed his/her first degree course and is below 25 years of age
may get himself/herself enrolled as a National Service Volunteer for one/two years.   The requirement of age and
educational qualification is relaxable in case of SC/ST and women volunteers.   Each of the volunteers enrolled under
the scheme is paid a stipend of Rs. 500/- per month and fixed travelling allowance @ Rs. 200/- per month.   They also
get a contingency grant of Rs. 100/- per year.   At present, the number of National Service Volunteers sanctioned is
5400.    The Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan, the National Service Scheme, State Governments and some reputed NGOs
are the implementing agencies.
5.2       The Committee was informed that the stipend /TA to NSVs has now been enhanced and fixed at par with NRC
Volunteers i.e. Rs. 1000/- While approving the enhancement of stipend for volunteers, EFC had imposed the condition
that this should be met from within the available budget allocation.   Thus, the BE/RE 2001-2002 and BE 2002-2003
have been kept at the same level i.e. Rs. 5.40 crores.   This may result in the reduction of the number of volunteers to be

recruited during 2002-2003.
5.3       The Committee notes that no unspent balance is lying with the implementing agencies for National Service
Volunteers Scheme, which are being instructed that no unspent balance will be adjusted as done in previous years and
fresh proposal for GIA will only be considered on refund of unspent amount in future.    The Committee, however, notes
with concern that even though EFC has given its approval for increase in honorarium for NSVS volunteer, it has
effectively reduced the impact of the scheme by stating that the increase has to be met within the available resources
which in turn will see a considerable reduction in the number of volunteers over a period of time.
VI        NATIONAL INTEGRATION PROGRAMME
6.1       This scheme provides the framework for greater exchange and understanding amongst the youth of the country
and greater involvement of voluntary agencies in the task  of national integration and communal harmony.   Two main
programmes which are covered under this scheme are:
(i)
                              National Integration Camp (NIC)  and
(ii)                            Inter-State Youth Exchange Programme (ISYEP)
6.2       The Committee was informed that the scheme of National Youth Award has since been merged with the scheme
of Promotion of National Integration.   The Committee notes that the Plan allocation has been reduced to Rs. 3.40 crores
in BE 2002-2003 from Rs. 4.50 crores in BE 2001-2002 and RE Rs. 4.00 crores.   Reduction in RE is due to less number
of applications for grant-in-aid.   As on 1.3.2002, expenditure of only Rs. 2.30 crores has been incurred under this
scheme.
6.3       Under the scheme of Promotion of National Integration, proposals are received from various State Govts. and
NGOs which are examined on merit and funds are released on finding them admissible in all respects.   The Committee 
notes that out of 258 National Integration Camps held during 2000-2001, none was held in NE States of Mizoram,
Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura, only one camp was held in each of the State of Meghalaya, Nagaland and Sikkim and
two camps in Assam.   Manipur is the only state where eight camps were held during this period.   The Committee notes
with constraint that the situation has deteriorated further during 2001-2002  with only one camp being approved for

the Committee understands that the Central Govt. also organizes such camps through its subordinate offices like the

lack of initiative on the part of the Central Govt. in holding such camps in uncovered areas like N-E region.   The
Central Govt. should pursue with the concerned State Govts. and NYKs and NSS units for holding the National
Integration camps there.    The Committee also feels that this scheme should be reviewed so as to assess its impact
specially in States/UTs like Bihar, UP, MP and Delhi where a very large number of camps have been held during 2000-
2001.
VII       YOUTH HOSTELS
7.1       Youth Hostels are built to promote youth travel and to enable the youth to experience the rich cultural heritage of
our country.   The scheme of Youth Hostels has been conceived as a joint venture of the Central and State Govts.  
While the Central Govt. bears the cost of construction, the State Govts.  provide developed plot of land equipped with
water, electricity and approach roads.   After completion, Youth Hostels are handed over to the State Govts. for
management.  
7.2       The Committee notes that so far 63 Youth Hostels have been constructed in different States.   Besides that, 21
Youth Hostels are under various stages of construction and 23 Youth Hostels have been approved in principle,
construction has yet to be started.   Undue delay in completion of construction process of Youth Hostels has been
engaging the attention of the Committee since last year.   From the details about 21 Youth Hostels under construction,
the Committee is shocked to learn that there are Youth Hostels approved as early as in 1986 where 1
st and even 2 nd
instalment of central funds for construction had been released at the earliest, with concerned State Govt taking ten years
in identifying suitable land for the Youth Hostel.   Construction of Youth Hostel in Lucknow was approved in principle 
on 21.8.87, and State Govt identified the land in 1998.   Three instalments of central funds amounting to Rs. 70.00 lakhs
released so far, with the first instalment released in March, 1988 and the construction is yet to be  completed.   Position
with regard to the remaining Youth Hostels is more or less the same.   So far as 23 Youth Hostels approved in principle
are concerned, the earliest dates back to 1986.   Not much progress, apart from correspondence with the State

VIII      NATIONAL RECONSTRUCTION CORPS SCHEME (NRC)
8.1       The scheme aims at providing an opportunity to Youth who are matriculate and attained the age of 18 years  to
participate in the process of nation building.   The NRC volunteers will be deployed by NYKS on specific projects
relating to community and national development.   The deployment of volunteers will be for one year and they will get a
stipend of Rs. 1,000/- p.m. exclusive of travel expenses. There would be sufficient representation of women and SC/ST
/OBC youth.  
8.2       Under the Scheme, a Project Officer and 100 Volunteers have been selected by a duly constituted committee for
each district and for 80 districts, 80 project officers and 8000 volunteers have been deployed by the NYKS.   Seven
schemes of the Government have been identified for implementation by the NRC Volunteers in the targeted districts.  
These are (i) Swarnjayant Gram Swarojgar Yojna, (ii) National Anti-Malaria Programme, (iii) Swarnjayanti Shahri
Rojgar Yojana (iv) Integrated Watershed Development, (v) Renewable Energy System, (vi) Social Forestry and (vii) 
Promotion of Literacy.   The Committee has been informed that this scheme has became operational from 1
st April,
2001 in 80 selected districts of the country.   Forty more districts will be added during the second year of its
operationalisation.   The scheme will be evaluated after the second year and depending on the outcome of the
evaluation, the Ministry proposes to extend this scheme to all the districts of the country, either as a Central Sector
Scheme or a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
8.3       The Committee hopes that the  scheme would fulfill its objectives. The Committee has, however, a word of
caution in view of different schemes relating to different Departments and Ministries sought to be implemented under
the umbrella of one single scheme.  The idea is a laudable one.  But the Department will have to play a pro-active role
by having proper co-ordination with all the Departments/Ministries and acting as the main linking force between the
implementing agency and the concerned Department.  The Committee would like to point out that a strong monitoring
mechanism also needs to be evolved from the very beginning for effective implementation of  the scheme of National
Reconstruction Corps.  The Committee also recommends that instead of launching all the targeted schemes in a
particular district simultaneously,  assessment should be made about their requirement and only thereafter schemes
should be implemented on priority basis.

10.1     Sports Authority of India (SAI) was established by the Government of India on the 16
th March, 1984 with the
twin objectives of spotting/nurturing talented children and striving for excellence.  SAI is also responsible for
maintaining and utilising stadia, which were constructed/renovated during IX Asian Games at Delhi.  SAI network
spans the length and breadth of the country through its headquarters at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, New Delhi and 6
Regional Centres.   SAI proposes to open 5 more Sub-Centres in addition to its Regional Centres. 
10.2     Sports Authority of India was provided a budget allocation of Rs. 81.33 crores under BE 2001-2002 which was
increased to Rs. 94.16 crores in RE to provide for the additional amount spent  on upgradation of Sports Authority of

has been kept at Rs. 88.23 crores which is higher by an amount of Rs. 6.90 crores over the BE 2001-2002.   The
Committee notes that the increase in SAI's budget is on account of creation of sports infrastructure, creation of new
centres/sub-centres, holding of continuous coaching camps as a part of preparation of teams and sportspersons for the
Commonwealth and Asian Games.  The Committee notes that against BE allocation of Rs. 81.33 crores in 2001-2002,
expenditure reported upto 1.3.2002 is only Rs. 65.99 crores.  The Committee hopes that allocation of Rs. 88.23 crores in

proper plan for maintaining of the buildings/stadia constructed at huge cost.

 OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS AT GLANCE

The Committee, however, notes that an expenditure of only Rs. 11.12 crores has been incurred upto 1.3.2002 against an
allocation of Rs. 23.23 crores in BE 2001-2002.   The Committee has been given to understand that during 2000-2001,
the last instalment  of GIA  was released to NYKS only in the last week of March, 2001 as the Utilisation Certificate
submitted by the Sangathan was not in an appropriate  format.   The Committee  apprehends that non-submission of
Utilisation Certificate and statement of  accounts within  the prescribed time limit must be one of the reasons for
expenditure of only one-third of the allocated funds under NYKS during 2001-2002.   The Committee would like to be
apprised about the factors responsible for such a discouraging trend.  (Para 3.8)
Annual Report for the year 2001-2002  highlights a variety of regular programmes like Youth Club
Development,  Awareness Generation, Vocational Training etc.    organised and seminars and workshops conducted by
various Nehru Yuva Kendras and on each programme/workshop etc.   funds ranging from Rs. 4,000 to Rs. 30,000 per
Kendra have been either allocated or earmarked.  The number of these programme/workshops must have increased by
the year end i.e. 31
st March, 2002.    The Committee strongly feels that either these achievements in majority of the
cases are on paper only or unspent balances are lying with  many Nehru Yuva Kendras.  Either way, it cannot be
considered an ideal position.    The Committee is of the view that the Department should not entirely depend on the
progress reports forwarded by the NYKS.   An effective  monitoring  mechanism  with an element of surprise 
inspections should be evolved.    It is understood that instructions have already been issued for associating the local
MPs/MLAs with the District Advisory Committee on Youth Programmes.    The Committee would like to be informed
within  a period of three months about the implementation of these instructions together with the details of the inter-
action with local MPs/MLAs.  (Para 3.9)
The Committee notes that a total of 492 district NYKs have District Advisory Committee for Youth Programme
(DACYPs) and for the remaining 8 districts, DACYPs are likely to be formed by the first quarter of 2002-2003.    The
Committee observes that against the prescribed 30% representation of women in DACYPs, national average comes to
36.47%.    The Committee is, however, constrained to point out that in some of the States/UTs, representation of
women  in DACYPs is much below the prescribed 30% .   For example in Lakshdweep, it is as low as 11.1% and in
West Bengal only 13.63%.    The Committee recommends that NYKS in such States/UTs. should be approached for
doing the needful in this regard. (Para 3.10)
The Committee hopes that these efforts would have the desired results. (Para 3.7)
IV        NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME (NSS)
The Committee would like to point out that although allocation of funds might have been less than the projected
requirements of the Department in 1999-2000 and 2000-2001, allocated funds had remained under-utilised.   Situation
seems to have worsened in 2001-2002.   Against allocation of Rs. 23.85 crores, only Rs. 9.15 crores have been utilised
upto 1.3.2002. (Para  4.3)
            While examining the Demands for Grants for 2000-2001, the Committee had expressed its serious concern over
non-settlement of accounts by a large number of States/UTs.  The Committee notes that since then, situation has
improved somewhat in respect of States like Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Mizoram, West Bengal,
Arunachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Chandigarh, Sikkim and Rajasthan.   However, in respect of the following
States, no improvement whatsoever has been made:
State A/cs. settled 1999-2000 A/cs. settled as on 15.2.2002
Assam 1979-80 1979-80
Delhi 1982-83 1982-83
Lakshwadweep 1983-84 1983-84
A.N. Islands 1979-80 1979-80
Jammu & Kashmir 1989-90 1989-90
The Committee observes that situation might have improved in respect of some States/UTs, but the fact remains
that pendency in settlement  of accounts is there more or less in respect of all States/UTs.   The Committee expresses its

122nd Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/122ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:28]
serious concern over this state of affairs specially in the case of above-mentioned States/UTs.   What is more shocking is
that implementing agencies under NSS are universities, colleges and +2 level schools and institutions of higher learning
and not NGOs lacking the required background.    The Committee finds it rather amazing that the Department has failed
to pursue the matter even with NCT of Delhi.  (Para 4.4)
             The Committee is constrained to note that unspent NSS Grants amounting to Rs. 25,12,84,195 are lying with
various State Govts./UTs  with Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Punjab, Rajasthan, UP, Gujarat and Maharashtra
being the major defaulters. As per the accounting procedure under NSS, funds are transferred from Central Govt. to
State Govts.   The State  Govts. after adding their  share of funds transfer this amount to the Universities/+2 level
schools which, in turn, transfer this amount to the NSS implementing units in colleges/schools.   The States/UTs submit
their accounts in the prescribed proforma indicating the details of central share and matching state share grants.   The
Committee has been informed that the present accounting procedure is working satisfactorily and there was no proposal
to revamp it.   The Committee is, however, not inclined to agree with the contention of the Ministry.   Had it been so,
huge amount of unspent NSS Grants would not have been lying with many States/UTs.   The Committee is of the firm
view that there is an urgent need to review the accounting procedure under NSS and the Department should initiate
action in this regard. (Para 4.5)
V         NATIONAL SERVICE VOLUNTEER SCHEME
            The Committee notes that no unspent balance is lying with the implementing agencies for National Service
Volunteers Scheme, which are being instructed that no unspent balance will be adjusted as done in previous years and
fresh proposal for GIA will only be considered on refund of unspent amount in future.    The Committee, however, notes
with concern that even though EFC has given its approval for increase in honorarium for NSVS volunteer, it has
effectively reduced the impact of the scheme by stating that the increase has to be met within the available resources
which in turn will see a considerable reduction in the number of volunteers over a period of time. (Para 5.3)
VI        NATIONAL INTEGRATION PROGRAMME
The Committee  notes that out of 258 National Integration Camps held during 2000-2001, none was held in NE
States of Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura, only one camp was held in each of the State of Meghalaya,
Nagaland and Sikkim and two camps in Assam.   Manipur is the only state where eight camps were held during this
period.   The Committee notes with constraint that the situation has deteriorated further during 2001-2002  with only
one camp being approved for Assam in the entire NE region and Sikkim.   While noting that every year about  75%
camps are organized by NGOs, the Committee understands that the Central Govt. also organizes such camps through its
subordinate offices like the NYKs and NSS units and also in collaboration with State Govts.    The Committee fails to
understand the reasons for lack of initiative on the part of the Central Govt. in holding such camps in uncovered areas
like N-E region.   The Central Govt. should pursue with the concerned State Govts. and NYKs and NSS units for
holding the National Integration camps there.    The Committee also feels that this scheme should be reviewed so as to
assess its impact specially in States/UTs like Bihar, UP, MP and Delhi where a very large number of camps have been
held during 2000-2001. (Para 6.3)
VII       YOUTH HOSTELS
Undue delay in completion of construction process of Youth Hostels has been engaging the attention of the
Committee since last year.   From the details about 21 Youth Hostels under construction, the Committee is shocked to
learn that there are Youth Hostels approved as early as in 1986 where 1
st and even 2 nd instalment of central funds for
construction had been released at the earliest, with concerned State Govt taking ten years in identifying suitable land for
the Youth Hostel.   Construction of Youth Hostel in Lucknow was approved in principle  on 21.8.87, and State Govt
identified the land in 1998.   Three instalments of central funds amounting to Rs. 70.00 lakhs released so far, with the
first instalment released in March, 1988 and the construction is yet to be  completed.   Position with regard to the
remaining Youth Hostels is more or less the same.   So far as 23 Youth Hostels approved in principle are concerned, the
earliest dates back to 1986.   Not much progress, apart from correspondence with the State Governments,  has been
made.   It seems that these proposals will continue to remain for another ten years or so.   The Committee notes that a
number of steps like writing letters to concerned State Chief Secretaries and entrusting of constructing work only to
CPWD have been taken by the  Department.   But the Committee does not find any noticeable impact of the same so
far.    The Committee would like to emphasise that drastic measures are required to be taken in the matter as with the
passage of time, estimates for construction would also keep on steadily increasing, thus leading to criminal wastage of

122nd Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/122ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:28]
Government funds. (Para 7.2)
VIII      NATIONAL RECONSTRUCTION CORPS SCHEME (NRC)
            The Committee hopes that the  scheme would fulfill its objectives. The Committee has, however, a word of
caution in view of different schemes relating to different Departments and Ministries sought to be implemented under
the umbrella of one single scheme.  The idea is a laudable one.  But the Department will have to play a pro-active role
by having proper co-ordination with all the Departments/Ministries and acting as the main linking force between the
implementing agency and the concerned Department.  The Committee would like to point out that a strong monitoring
mechanism also needs to be evolved from the very beginning for effective implementation of  the scheme of National
Reconstruction Corps.  The Committee also recommends that instead of launching all the targeted schemes in a
particular district simultaneously,  assessment should be made about their requirement and only thereafter schemes
should be implemented on priority basis. (Para 8.3)
IX        PROMOTION OF YOUTH ACTIVITIES AND TRAINING
The Committee is, however, constrained to note that not much progress seems to have been made during 2001-
2002.  The Committee notes that the Planning Commission have approved the merger of these schemes as part of the
zero-based budgeting exercise and the Ministry of Finance are now being approached to convey their approval.  The
Committee urges upon the Department to expedite the completion of all the formalities so that the new composite
scheme could be activated during 2002-2003.  (Para 9.2)
The Committee notes that there is a long list of such NGOs having Govt. funds lying with them from 1997-98
onwards as detailed in the Annual Report of the Ministry for 2001-2002.  The Committee would like to quote two
examples.  Under the earlier scheme of `Financial Assistance to Voluntary Organisations working in the Field of Youth’
as many as 40 NGOs in Bihar are yet to submit Utilization Certificates pertaining to more then  Rs. 52.00 lakhs since
1999-2000.  Likewise from UP, 48 NGOs are having funds amounting to more that Rs. 75.00 lakhs with them since
1999-2000.  The Committee has been given to understand that action has been taken to stop further Grants to such
NGOs and the matter is being actively pursued with them.  The Committee does not have much faith in this exercise. 
The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation that all the inherent flaws particularly relating to handling of
earlier schemes by NGOs should not be reflected in the revised scheme.  At the same time, the Committee fails to
understand as to how NGOs not having the proper antecedents are released Govt. funds for running different schemes. 
The Committee strongly feels that there is an urgent need for having an element of accountability at every level –
Centre/State/district.  Only then, things might improve.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that a fool proof
mechanism for selection of NGOs should be put into practice.  Efforts should also be made to avoid concentration of
many NGOs in one particular  district. (Para 9.3)
The Committee hopes that all the preliminary formalities for these two proposed schemes have been completed.
(Para 9.4)
X         SPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
The Committee hopes that allocation of Rs. 88.23 crores in BE 2002-2003 would not remain under utilised.
(Para 10.2)
10.3     The Committee hopes that all the infrastructure created would be optimally utilized and there should also be
proper plan for maintaining of the buildings/stadia constructed at huge cost. (Para 10.3)
XI        SPECIAL AREA GAMES (SAG) SCHEME
            The Committee would like to be apprised about the progress made in this matter.  The Committee hopes that the
State Govt. of Orissa must have handed over the Sankara Sports complex for establishment of a full fledged SAG
Centre at Sundargarh during 2002-2003.  If not done, the Ministry should make all efforts to expedite the same.  The
Committee strongly feels that the Sports Authority of India should make a special endeavour to activate such proposals
whenever brought to its notice. (Para 11.3)
XII       ALL INDIA COUNCIL FOR PHYSICAL EDUCATION
The Committee is not in favour of allocating a token provision for a yet to be approved scheme.  General trend
noticed by the Committee in such matters is that token provision is made year after year with the scheme continuing in a
proposal stage.  The Committee is of the strong view that only after completing all the requisite preliminary formalities

122nd Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/122ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:28]
for launching a new scheme, provision of funds should be made  for the same. (Para 12.1)
XIII      INCENTIVE SCHEMES
It is understood that these schemes are proposed to be brought under one composite scheme.  The Committee
welcomes the initiative as, by and large,  these schemes have failed to achieve their targets during Ninth Plan period. 
The Committee strongly feels that there is a need for giving wide publicity to such incentive schemes so that the
targeted persons can get the maximum benefit thereunder.  The Committee , therefore, recommends that the Ministry
should make concerted efforts in this direction. (Para 13)
XIV     GRANTS TO NATIONAL SPORTS FEDERATIONS.
The Committee has been given to understand that these federations being autonomous organisations, Govt. have
very little say in their affairs.  The Committee, however, is of the view that as Govt. funding is there, there has to be an
element of accountability also.  Out of 50 federations provided financial assistance during 2001-2002, allocations range
from Rs. 23,750 to Rs. 1,91,17,000.  The Committee strongly feels that submission of quarterly progress reports should
be made a pre-condition  for further release of funds.  The Committee finds that School Games Federation of India and
Tug of War Federation of India were provided Rs. 18,72,809 and Rs. 10,00,000 respectively in 2001-2002.  The
Committee would like to have an idea about the activities of these federations.  The Committee recommends that an
exercise for reviewing and evaluating the work done by all federations should also be initiated.  Such an exercise is
likely to clear the picture about the inherent flaws in the system and also come up with suggestions for improvement.     
(Para 14.3)
XV       GRANT FOR CREATION OF SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE
The Committee finds that the main reason for such a situation is that some States have not incurred their share of
expenditure with the result the Department could not release the Central Govt’s share as the scheme prescribes incurring
of State Govt’s share  first.  Last year, the Committee noticed that 274 sports infrastructure projects sanctioned from
1990 onwards till 28.2.01 were in various stages of construction.  The  Committee has been apprised that during the
period 1998-2001, 65 projects have been completed after a lot of persuasion and constant correspondence.  The
Committee, however, feels that this has not made any  significant change in the number of pending projects.  The
Committee is not aware about the number of projects completed during 2001-2002.  The Committee has been given to
understand that no time limit has been prescribed under the scheme for completion of projects, indication of one  to two
years’ time for completion indicated in the application form and provision regarding claiming assistance within two
years in the approval letter notwithstanding.  The Committee is of the firm view that adherence to the time limit by both
the implementing agencies and the Ministry would have shown a better record.  These over-delayed projects have
virtually defeated the very purpose of launching of the scheme for Creation of Sports Infrastructure. (Para 15.2)
XVI     GRANT FOR INSTALLATION OF SYNTHETIC PLAYING SURFACES
            During the Ninth Plan period, allocation of funds and utilization thereof under this scheme has shown a
declining trend.  The Committee observes that situation has been very discouraging during 2001-2002, the last year of
the Ninth Plan.  Allocation of Rs. 5.40 crores was reduced to Rs. 3.85 crores at the RE stage and expenditure reported
upto 1.3.2002 is only Rs. 43 lakhs.  The Committee notes that the main reason for under-utilization of funds under this
scheme has been the difficulty being faced in providing the matching in share as well as failure of user agencies
furnishing the progress report and utilization certificates of the already approved projects.  The Committee has been
informed that during Ninth Plan, 16 synthetic hockey surfaces and 6 synthetic athletic tracks in different parts of the
country have been approved with Central assistance of Rs. 20.22 crores and the balance of Rs. 9.66 crores payable for
these projects.  The Committee has no other alternative but to conclude that the approval of 22 projects under the
scheme of `Grant for Installation of Synthetic Playing Surface’ indicates a very dismal picture as apparently not even a
single could be completed and put to effective use during the Ninth Plan period.  The Committee strongly urges the
Ministry to expedite the completion of all these pending projects without any further delay. (Para 16.2)
The Committee hopes that there will be no further delay in the launching of the revised scheme pertaining
to infrastructure. (Para 16.3)
XVII    NEW SCHEMES
            The Committee appreciates the idea and hopes that State Governments/ Corporate Sponsors will be able to
contribute their respective share in due time to make the scheme of State Sports Academies a success.   The Committee

122nd Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/122ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:28]
feels that the Scheme for Dope Test should be operationalised and strictly implemented  if the country wants to have a
name in the international arena.  The Committee, however, has its doubts about the possibility of launching of these two
schemes during 2002-2003 due to various procedural formalities yet to be gone through.  The Committee, therefore,
urges upon the Ministry to expedite all necessary measures so as to ensure that the schemes are launched at the earliest.
(Para 17.2)

INTRODUCTION
 
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource Development,
having been authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, present this Hundred-Twenty Third Report
of the Committee relating to the Infant Milk Substitutes,  Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods    (Regulation of Production,
Supply and Distribution) Amendment Bill, 2002*. (Annexure-I)
2.         In pursuance of Rule 270 relating to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees, the Chairman,
Rajya Sabha, in consultation with the Speaker, Lok Sabha referred** the Infant Milk Substitutes,  Feeding Bottles and

The Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods    (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution)
Amendment Bill, 2002, seeks to amend sections 2,3,4,5,7,9,20 and 24 of the Infant Milk Substitutes,  Feeding Bottles
and Infant Foods    (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992, so as to encourage continued
breastfeeding and to prohibit all forms of advertising and promotion -- light, sound, smoke or gas or by means of
electronic transmission  by audio or visual transmission in relation to Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant
Foods.
2.         The Statement of Objects and Reasons appended to the Bill  is placed at Annexure IV
:
The Secretary, Department of Women and Child Development in his presentation on the Bill inter alia  stated:
"Basically, the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods    (Regulation of Production, Supply and
Distribution) Act, 1992 was enacted with a view to ensuring that there is no misrepresentation by companies that these
milk substitutes are  better than breast milk because, scientifically, it has been established that from the nutritional point
of view, in the first few months of infancy, there is no substitute for breast milk.   There is a lot of international and
national evidence in this regard.   We started with an Indian National Code in 1983, but it was felt that this was not
adequate and that there should be a statutory basis.   Then, the Act of 1992 came.   Basically, this Act has a lot of
prescriptions and prohibitions, how this should not be permitted - infant food and  infant milk substitutes- to the

detriment  of breast milk.   There are restrictions on labelling, advertising etc.  In the last 10 years there have been
further studies within the country and outside and now the considered technical opinion is that breast milk is preferred
for the first six months, instead of four months earlier, and thereafter, as far as possible, it should be continued for a
period of two years.  After the first six months, complementary food should be provided.
Another major happening that has happened is  the definition of advertisement has changed in the light of the various
developments which has taken place due to cable T.V.,  Satellite channels and electronic transmission.  Similarly, in
actual practice, it was noticed that apart from the healthcare workers in the hospitals, in the pharmacies, a lot of
propagation was being  done in favour of Infant Foods and Infant Milk Substitutes.  Therefore, a lot of minor
modifications have been brought in, with reference to advertisement, with reference to supplies, and with reference to
taking part in promotion".

The Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods    (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution)
Act, 1992 was enacted with a view to protecting and promoting breastfeeding and ensuring proper use of infant foods.   
During the course of implementation of the provisions of the enactment over the years, it has been found that some
aspects have led to difficulties, which need to be clearly spelt out.   The recent developments and findings of
international agencies as well as researchers have revealed that ideally, the infant thrives best on exclusive breastfeeding
for the first six months of life, as well as continued breastfeeding together with complementary foods for the first two
years.   The World Health Organisation by World Health Assembly Resolution No. 47.5 dated the 9
th May, 1994 called
upon all Member Nations to aim at achieving this goal.   The said resolution, inter alia,  required Member Nations to
foster appropriate complementary feeding practices for the infants from the age of about six months and encourage
continued breastfeeding as well as proper feeding with safe and adequate amounts of local foods until the infant attains
the age of two years.
In order to review and suggest appropriate amendments in the said Act, the Department of Women and Child

Development, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, present this 
Hundred-Twenty Fourth Report of the Committee.  The report is  on the Protection from Domestic 
Violence Bill, 2002*.  
2.         In 
pursuance of Rule 270 relating to the Department related Parliamentary Standing Committees,

REPORT 
  
            The Protection from Domestic Violence Bill, 2002, seeks to protect the rights of women who are 
victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family and to provide for matters connected 
therewith or incidental thereto. 
The Statement of Objects and Reasons appended to the Bill states as under:  
“Domestic violence is undoubtedly a human rights issue and serious deterrent to development.  The 
Vienna Accord of 1994 and the Beijing Platform of Action (1995) both have acknowledged this.  The 
United Nations Committee on CEDAW (Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination 
Against Women) in its general recommendation No. XII (1989) has recommended that State parties 
should act to protect women against violence of any kind especially that occurring within the family.  
The phenomenon of domestic violence is widely prevalent but has remained largely invisible in the 
public domain.  Presently, where a woman is visited with cruelty by her husband or his relatives is an 
offence under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. The civil law does not address this 
phenomenon in its entirety.   
With a view to providing a remedy under the civil law, which is intended to preserve the family and at 
the same time provide protection to victims of domestic violence, legislation is being proposed.  The 
main features as contained in the Bill are as follows:- 
it is being provided that any conduct of relative of the victim, which subjects her to habitual assault, or 
makes her life miserable, or injures or harms, or forces her to lead an immoral life would constitute 
domestic violence; 
the Judicial Magistrate of the first class or the Metropolitan Magistrate may take the cognizance of 
domestic violence and pass a protection order requiring the relative of the women to refrain from 
committing an act of domestic violence, or pay monetary relief which is deemed fit in the circumstances 
or pass any other direction as the Magistrate may consider just; 
the Magistrate may even require as an interim and urgent measure from the relative of the woman to 
execute a bond, with or without sureties, for maintaining domestic peace; 
the violation by the relative of the order made by the Magistrate would constitute an offence punishable 
with imprisonment up to one year, or with fine, or with both; 
it is being proposed to set up an institution of Protection Officer to help the victim of domestic violence 
in making application to the Magistrate and in availing of her other legal rights; 
a provision is being made for the appointment of Protection Officers  by State Governments and they 
shall possess such qualifications as may be prescribed by the Central Govt., and 
Protection Officer shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian 
Penal Code, 1860 and if he fails or refuses to discharge the duties as directed by the Magistrate, his act 
shall amount to an offence punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or with fine, or with both”. 
  
NEW DELHI   
3rd December, 2002      
ARJUN SINGH 
 Chairman 
Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Human Resource Development
